Etheric Sea: after crossing the Veil a ship too heavily loaded to move says so ("You're going to need a bigger boat"), where the crossing banner used to hide it, and everything carried, gold and wagon included, counts against a ship's hold

Morrowind People: the horses that stand in towns, at World of Daggerfall's bandit camps and forts and in the Stables stand as the 3D horse when Morrowind data is attached (the nearest eight within 60 m)

Morrowind People: people who used to stay as sprites now stand in Morrowind bodies: a town's figures that belong to no faction, World of Daggerfall's dock people, the captives, merchants and prisoners its markers place, and the crews on Come Sail Away's boats
Morrowind People: past the body range Daggerfall's own sprites still stand, as do other animals, children, vampires' people and Daedra Princes

Privateer's Hold: Privateer's Hold is no longer a private copy for each character but a shared dungeon like every other, with the same enemies, doors, levers and loot for everyone inside, and other players can be seen, chatted with and partied with there

Privateer's Hold: once the player leaves the Hold online they cannot go back in: its door, a Recall to a spot marked inside it and a quest that would send them there all say "You cannot go back into Privateer's Hold." and a Recall or quest arrival lands outside instead
Privateer's Hold: a new game still starts inside the Hold and a character saved inside it still loads back in
Privateer's Hold: offline, nothing changes

Furniture Stores: Furniture Stores show in the shop colour on both town maps, where they used to be drawn as houses, and like every other shop are named once the player has been inside or someone has marked it
Furniture Stores: townspeople can be asked where Furniture Stores are, from a new "Furniture stores" group in the Where-is list

Joinery: every city and town has a Joinery beside its Stables and Wagon Yard, room permitting, a carpenter's open-air yard with a shingled workshop, a timber rack, a log pile, sawhorses and a chopping block and a table, chairs and a bench on show by the gate

Joinery: its workbench is a Carpentry station, opened by talking to the carpenter or using the sign or the bench, which opens the Stores page at The Workbench, with a craft or a saw costing 50 gold as at a Furniture Store's bench and carpentry still done online
Furniture Stores: linen for beds is still sold only at Furniture Stores
Joinery: a Joinery can be found by asking townspeople under "Carpenters", on either town map, or by the saw mark on the Overworld map

Performance: entering the world freezes for less, since the game no longer stalls while working out where every town's pilgrims go for their holy days or picking the day's elite halls in the Wrothgarian zone, which stay the same
World Map: opening the map for the first time in a session takes 0.7 s on a desktop instead of 6.7 s

Ships: ships far out at sea, including those other players leave behind on logging off, no longer keep a full animated hull far away and decide less often while nobody can see them, with their voyages, fights and damage carrying on as before
Overworld: ships, their map lookups and wagon harness ropes do the same work for less effort and memory garbage, so walking the overworld coast runs faster
Horse: meeting a horse with a new coat on the road no longer freezes the game, as the coat is painted a few pictures at a time instead of all forty at once
Wagon: a parked team's harness stops recomputing its ropes while nothing moves
Desktop App: the app no longer reads the account and settings files from disk every frame but keeps them in memory as the browser does, giving smoother frames in a town

Yard: player yards take far fewer draw calls, each yard's 3D pieces drawn together and its repeated sprites drawn as one, so a town with decorated yards in view makes about 17-18% fewer draw calls a frame, helping most in the browser version and on weaker CPUs and drivers

Spells: online, a Destruction mastered past 100 adds to Damage Health and Continuous Damage spells, 1% for each point of its effective value past 100 and +40% at 200, where those points only made spells cheaper before; gear that raises Destruction still makes spells cheaper

Skill Training: a spell landing on a foe, or a foe's spell landing on the player, counts the foe being fought when training a mastered school past 100, so blasting a tough foe trains the school as fast as fighting it with a weapon, and a cast never trains slower than before
Loot Rarity: a new line, Potency, on jewellery and weapons gives +3% to +15% spell damage, with everything worn adding up to at most +30%
Loot Rarity: a new jewellery line, Wellspring, returns 2% to 10% of magicka when a foe is killed, at most 10% a kill from everything worn

Loot Rarity: The Eye of Magnus (amulet) with Magnus's Gaze makes Destruction spells meet a saving throw 15 lower, and a foe immune to the element stays immune, found most often among mages, covens and laboratories
Loot Rarity: The Ring of Artaeum (ring) with Wellspring of Artaeum returns 1% of magicka every magic round and 2% while under half
Loot Rarity: Shalidor's Brand (broadsword, saber or longsword) with Arcane Surge makes Destruction spells strike 25% harder while wielded and magicka is above three quarters
Loot Rarity: spell damage from loot is capped at +50% all together, and none of the new spell damage reaches a fight against another player
Werewolf: the beast's claws no longer count as silver, so creatures needing a better metal, such as a Lich or an Ancient Lich, take full damage from claws again

Werewolf: in beast form, plate gauntlets add their metal's damage bonus to every claw hit in every fight, duels and sieges included (Elven +1, Dwarven +2, Mithril and Adamantium +3, Ebony +4, Orcish +5, Daedric +6), the same bonus a weapon of that metal gets, with hit chance unchanged

Werewolf: leather and chain gauntlets add nothing, nor do brigandine gloves (which count as leather) or broken gauntlets, no gauntlets ever make claws weaker, and they must be put on before changing since the beast cannot open its pack
Werewolf: loading a save while in beast form no longer leaves the loaded character treated as a beast until the game is restarted, which kept townspeople from stopping for them
Elites: online, elite enemies no longer appear in the wilds or rise from searched graves until the character reaches Renown 5

Revenants: online, revenants wait for Renown 10: below it no foe becomes a revenant or breaks and runs to become one and none comes back, while existing revenants are held and marked Held on the Revenants page with when they will come
Revenants: revenants come back a little less often, a revenant that is due now taking 2 in 5 encounter chances instead of 1 in 2

Accounts: most menus that talk to the server load much faster (the Guild tab, the market, the Seat tab, letters, the account card and signing in), since the account server now runs next to its database instead of across the Pacific
Accounts: joining the world, the chat's player list and the friends list come up sooner after signing in, because each connection waits on the account server for its pass

Name in Game: a Name in game choice in the Account section of the profile card picks Account name or Character name, and with Character name other players see the playing character's name over their head, in chat and in the online list
Name in Game: the change shows within moments in every room the player is in, without changing area or signing in again

Name in Game: if the character's name cannot be shown online, other players see the account name instead and the chat says why once, which happens when the name is longer than 24 characters, uses accented letters or symbols, is caught by the name filter, looks like an email address or is another player's username
Name in Game: a letter sent from the friends list reaches the friend even when they go by their character's name
Name in Game: answering a notice-board duel finds its author even when they go by their character's name
Chat Window: titles no longer appear in chat, while guild tags and glyphs still show after names and the title still shows over the head and on the Inspect card
Letters of Credit: online, a letter of credit cannot be put into a chest, cupboard or body, since a shared container is everyone's, so it stays in the pack and is given to another player in a trade
Letters of Credit: the player's own storage (house cupboards, ship's chest), a pile they dropped themselves and the wagon still take letters, and nothing changes offline
Letters of Credit: outside a trade a letter of credit never reaches the player through another player's game, covering a shared chest, a body they let the player loot and a foe's pack handed over

Letters of Credit: a letter of credit already lying in a shared chest or on a body when the update arrived is gone from it, since anyone could take it before and the game cannot tell it from a forged one
Prices: an item that reaches the player through another player's game (a chest, a body, a shelf) cannot carry a higher price than an honest item of its kind could
Online Death: the gear a fallen player leaves in the wilds holds only things that can be worn

Player Trade: a purse, letter of credit or pile of gold holding more than 2,147,483,647 gold (more than Daggerfall itself can count) is flagged as tampered, and that character cannot trade, sell or send gold to other players until the problem is gone or staff clear it

Town Watch: when a monster attacks in town the guards still come to help but now walk off after the fight instead of vanishing on the spot about ten seconds later, and only leave the world once far away or behind the player, the same rule that hides townspeople coming and going

Town Watch: if another monster turns up while the guards are walking off, the same guards turn back to the fight instead of a fresh squad appearing, and a guard attacked on his way out defends himself before carrying on
Horse: a horse walks by default and holding Run (Shift unless rebound) gallops it, the same way the player walks and runs on foot
Horse: the gallop is as fast as before and still spends the horse's breath, and a winded or starving horse walks even with Run held until it can gallop again
Horse: in towns the horse walks because Roleplay & Realism does not allow galloping there, and the Galloping In Towns option under Enhanced Riding allows it
Horse: a walking horse looks and sounds like one, with a slower clop, a slower nod of its head in first person and a trot rather than a gallop on the 3D horse, and the saddle panel says Walking
Horse: with Horse care turned off in Settings > Features, or on the classic interface, horses ride as they always did

Elite Dungeons: walking past a spawned or Elite dungeon no longer starts its despawn timer (7 in-game days, about 14 real hours online), which starts only when someone enters, so a dungeon nobody goes into stays where it is
Elite Dungeons: a dungeon that has despawned comes back 24 real hours later, the same dungeon in the same spot with fresh timers, so emptied regions repopulate
Elite Dungeons: a character's save no longer keeps despawned dungeons gone forever, so players who walked an area weeks ago see the same dungeons as everyone else
Wrothgarian Zone: Wild Zone halls no longer vanish partway through their day after someone has been inside one
Quests: quest enemies, like the Fighters Guild's rats, now appear in shops, not only in houses
Quests: "Open a Chest" and other quests whose shop is in another town show that town in the quest list, on the travel map and on the compass
Homes: a home's chests no longer lose their contents when furniture fails to load, anything without a chest or box to go in being set down at the player's feet
Loot Rarity: the Gauntlets of the Rose's second hit lands on the Oblivion Gate's boss
Motherlodes: Motherlodes appear on the compass from their warning onward, in their own colour, drawn over nearby veins
Houses: windows no longer show the street where the building's own wall stands
Morrowind Models: Morrowind models (the player, NPCs, enemies and horses) no longer turn invisible until restart
Keybindings: Swing Weapon bound to Left Click, with mouse activate unbound, survives a restart

Water Surface: inland water banks (ponds, moats, rivers, streams, town canals) no longer show flat blue blotches on the grass beside the water, as the shore's painted water sits under the riverbed and the strip past the edge reads as dark wet mud
Water Surface: standing on a bank, the player can no longer see under the water's surface, as the water's edge meets the ground instead of floating over a dip
Boons: Climates & Calories has a fourth setting, Boons, between Off and Casual, and it is the default, so a player who never picked a setting plays Boons while a chosen Off, Hard or Casual is kept
Boons: Boons takes nothing away: keeping the character fed, watered and rested earns bonuses instead
Boons: Well fed gives +5 Strength and +5 Endurance
Boons: Quenched gives +5 Agility and +5 Speed
Boons: Well rested gives +5 Intelligence and +5 Willpower, with sleeping in a bed or by a fire banking rest of up to 12 hours that is spent while awake
Boons: Thriving, all three at once, gives +5 Luck
Boons: Hearth: standing by a lit fire gives stamina back
Boons: boons show as green tiles on the status strip, and nothing turns red in Boons except a drink's effect
Boons: on the Status page the hours of rest banked are a line of their own ("Rested for another 12 hours."), so the classic status box no longer grows wider for them
Resting: online, the tile that counts down until the player can sleep through a night again is called "Next night", where it was "Rested", easily mistaken for Well rested

Temperature Display: a temperature plate at the right end of the compass (Enhanced HUD) shows the felt temperature, its word and a scale from deadly cold to scorching, staying on screen at every HUD scale and on phones clear of the FPS counter, enemy health bar, arena session button and travel pace box, movable and hideable on its own, still shown when the compass is hidden, and switched off by "Temperature on the HUD" in the Climates & Calories settings

Temperature Display: the Enhanced inventory shows the felt temperature beside the armour rating, an item's card says what wearing or removing it would do to the temperature, and an unidentified item's comparison no longer counts powers not yet visible
Temperature Display: the Stats side lists everything that makes up the temperature, and the Status page shows the number

Temperature Display: red now means the setting played on charges for it and amber means it is felt but costs nothing, with every costly need red in Hard, being wet amber in every setting and each level also said in words
Climates & Calories: Resist Fire no longer makes a blizzard colder and Resist Frost no longer makes the desert hotter, and underground resistances act on the dungeon's own air
Climates & Calories: swimming on the surface soaks a little at a time and only going under soaks at once, so a short river swim no longer leaves the player drenched for hours
Climates & Calories: rain and snow soak at the original mod's rates, with a cloak keeping snow off and a hood keeping rain off
Climates & Calories: robes and cloaks keep the sun off the armour, while surcoats and straps no longer do because they are worn under it
Climates & Calories: underground, clothes, metal armour and food follow the dungeon's air, not the weather above it
Climates & Calories: warm weather takes effect on clothing and a hood's shade gradually, so a slightly warmer day no longer reads much colder
Climates & Calories: indoors, a warmer street no longer reads colder inside
Climates & Calories: having a drink to hand cools the player down to 9 degrees at most, instead of dropping them to 0
Climates & Calories: cold metal armour chills a degree less, as in the original mod
Climates & Calories: the temperature number and its word always agree, and the breakdown's "Bare skin" row is now called "Heat loss"
Climates & Calories: the open sea is no longer as warm as a beach, so a winter crossing is cold
Climates & Calories: offline, a long rest or a fast-travel journey feels each hour as it passes, including the minute of arrival, with cold nights, warm noons and sun only by day
Climates & Calories: a long journey no longer keeps the weather it set out in all the way, the road being felt under a fair sky
Climates & Calories: in a castle the Stats breakdown names the row "Castle walls" instead of "Underground"
Climates & Calories: in Hard, a long fast-travel journey can no longer collapse the player from exhaustion over and over on the way, or kill them in the minute they land
Climates & Calories: collapsing from exhaustion counts as an hour's sleep on the ground
Climates & Calories: saving partway through a fast-travel journey is no longer possible ("You cannot save now."), the online checkpoint waiting until arrival
Climates & Calories: leaving prison, the player starts fed, watered and rested, not starving, soaked and exhausted
Climates & Calories: a cured vampire is no longer instantly starving and exhausted, and a werewolf in beast form neither hungers nor thirsts
Climates & Calories: stamina no longer stays above its maximum after a boon or a Fortify ends
Climates & Calories: survival messages no longer repeat when the player steps in and out of a fire's reach, and loading a game no longer repeats them all
Climates & Calories: bare feet are hurt by the weather's own heat or cold, before clothes count, measured against current Endurance so Fortify Endurance helps, and are no longer hurt underground
Campfire: resting at the player's own burnt-out Campfire relights it if it has fuel, and a worn-out tent no longer claims to stoke its fire
Tents: sleeping in the tent keeps the rain and snow off, and armour no longer rusts while resting or under a roof
Campfire: a cold camp no longer offers Cook
Campfire: resting at a brazier or fire bowl needs the player within the fire's reach, and from further away they are told to move closer instead of getting a rough night's rest
Campfire: a campfire on a ship's deck no longer counts as a fire while the ship is out of sight
Climates & Calories: food that spoils in the pack shows its spoiled name and picture, and putrid food says it cannot be eaten
Climates & Calories: new characters start with the original mod's Formal cloak, hood up, and Shoes, both well worn
Climates & Calories: an empty waterskin from a shop is called "Empty Waterskin"
Climates & Calories: tavern menus follow the original mod's regional menus, prices and holiday free drinks
Climates & Calories: a meal ordered when nearly full is served whole and leaves the player fed
Climates & Calories: a soft drink refreshes (+5 stamina) and an alcoholic drink restores stamina and magicka
Climates & Calories: online, passing out drunk wakes the player at the next dawn under the sky everyone shares
Duels: Boons and other buffs count properly in duels, sieges and the Royal Tourney, where the player's own attributes and Luck were counted against them

Climbing: in first person (classic view) the hands stay on the wall when climbing or hanging, sliding across with the stone when the view turns and going down the wall when looking up, instead of turning with the screen
Climbing: the two fists grip further apart, about shoulder width

Climbing: when looking away from the wall to find the next jump, the arm that reaches out is the one on the side looked, right arm from the right and left arm from the left, and only that arm stays fixed to the screen while its hand lets go of the wall and the other keeps its hold
Morrowind Body: with the Morrowind model in first person, the arms grip the wall while climbing even with the weapon sheathed, where the screen showed nothing unless a weapon was drawn
Weapon Widget: Weapon Widget's bob and sway no longer push the Morrowind hands off the stone while they climb
Horse: a horse no longer has to walk in towns: it still walks by default and holding Run gallops it anywhere, in town or out, as long as it has the breath, online too
Horse: riding into someone at a gallop in town tramples them, which is a crime and brings the guards

Front Door: on a handheld held sideways, like the ASUS ROG Xbox Ally X, the logo no longer fills the screen and the menu keeps its two columns (sections down the side and the open page at full height), so Settings, Load, Online and the rest can be used again, and a narrowed desktop browser window gets the same layout

Language: Settings > Interface > Language offers 13 languages besides English (Bulgarian, Czech, Danish, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese (Brazil), Romanian, Russian and Spanish), applied at once and remembered, and if the browser reads one of them first the game offers it once in that language

Language: the translations cover the game's own menus and screens (the front door and Settings, the pause window, the death screens, account and online messages, the Professions and Stores pages and every crafting station, the Features screen and every mod's settings) and are machine translated, which the game says, with more languages on the way

Translation Packs: under the Language row, Translation pack installs a Daggerfall Unity translation (a folder or its .zip) from the player's own files without uploading anything, translating Daggerfall's own text too (dialogue, quests, books and the names of places, enemies, items and spells) and working for a language not in the list, with the French pack's grammar working
Language: the classic windows draw any script (Cyrillic, Greek, Vietnamese, Chinese, Japanese and Korean), where anything past plain English letters came out as question marks
Language: the About pane credits each language's translation

Morrowind Models: players, NPCs and horses no longer turn invisible online with Morrowind models: a bad position for one body (for example from another player's glitched update) used to vanish every body drawn after it until that player left or the game restarted, and now only that one body stays at its last good position

Crime: pleading guilty no longer loops, as the plea now waits until the Crime tutorial page on top of it has been read, where clicking Guilty or Not Guilty under the page answered the plea beneath and every click pleaded again, took the fine again and halved the sentence again
Etheric Sea: the Overworld can be risen into while sailing the Eltheric Ocean, as in the Iliac Bay, by pressing Overworld (O) on the chart or O while the chart is open

Etheric Sea: from the Overworld past the Veil, clicking the sea sails there at the helm and clicking a charted port or ruin travels to it, with farther charted ports shown at the screen edge with their distance and ruins appearing as a "?" until charted or found
Etheric Sea: an island charted by sight, a harbourmaster's chart or a corsair's papers shows on the Overworld at once without moving first
Etheric Sea: a fast journey past the Veil slows while the land ahead is still loading, so the player no longer outruns the world

Etheric Sea: enemy bands roam the Eltheric isles and, with Naval Combat on, pirate raiders sail its open sea, shown on the Overworld as in the Bay, chasing the same way and slowing the journey as they close in

Etheric Sea: a raider past the Veil comes as one of the Eltheric's own corsairs, a ship fought at sea with the sea's names, the black flag and a hold as rich as the waters she sails, and for a newer captain the deeper the water the bigger the ship she may be
Etheric Sea: online, other players see a band or raider chasing the player past the Veil

Etheric Sea: the sea past the Veil is called the Eltheric Ocean, its proper name, where it used to be called the "Etheric Sea", across the chart, harbourmasters, the crossing, the captain's log and the legends

Etheric Sea: the water past the Veil has a real seabed, shallow by each island's shore and dropping to the open ocean floor about two hundred metres down, as deep as the Iliac Bay's open sea, where it used to be only a stride deep
Etheric Sea: the player can swim, dive and surface past the Veil as in the Bay, and the seafloor's plants, fish, creatures and sunken loot appear there too
Etheric Sea: the ocean holes (the pits down into drowned dungeons) still appear only in the Iliac Bay
Gathering: herbs, trees, ore veins and boulders on the islands past the Veil can be gathered, where they used to answer "There is nothing here to gather", and fishing in the Eltheric Ocean works too
Gathering: gathering past the Veil works as in the Bay, each spot giving its full finds only once three players with accounts at least a week old have gathered there
Motherlodes: Motherlodes still rise only in the Iliac Bay, where the Watch can see the player strike them
Sea Chart: the chart's names are in the game's own enhanced font, where they used to be drawn in a fallback serif
Sea Chart: names are drawn after every island marker with a dark outline, so a marker can no longer cover a name
Sea Chart: each name sits on whichever side of its island is clear, names and haunt labels no longer stand over each other, and the player's ship label takes the clearest spot
Sea Chart: a depth ruler along the top of the chart names each stretch of water in view with room for its name: the Shallows, the Reaches, the Deep Aether, the Abyss, the Veil and the world's edge
Sea Chart: the scale bar sits in the key below the chart, so it no longer hides islands

Sea Chart: the chart's words follow the chosen language in each fully translated language, while the sea's own names (the Eltheric Ocean, its depths, island types and compass directions) are still in English for now
Sea Chart: each island type has its own shape as well as its own colour, so ruins and wild isles no longer differ by red and green alone
Sea Chart: a port is round with a harbour dot
Sea Chart: a ruin is a diamond
Sea Chart: a wild isle is a peak
Sea Chart: a bare rock is a cross
Sea Chart: zooming in shows larger islands at their real size around the icon, and Veilhaven is ringed in gold
Sea Chart: a key under the chart explains every icon

Sea Chart: each depth band is its own shade of water, lightest by the Veil and darkest in the Abyss, a league grid replaces the old background stars that did not move when dragged, and the edge of the world is marked

Sea Chart: a legend's haunt is a red-washed square while she sails and hatched grey while she lies sunk, with her name and status ("Her haunt", "Sunk - she will rise again") in a corner when enough of the square is in view and her name alone above it when zoomed far out
Sea Chart: the player's ship is a white arrow in a brass ring, marked on the ruler too, and when off-screen an arrow at the chart's edge points to her and says how far away she is
Sea Chart: pointing at or tapping an island rings it, draws a bearing line to it from the ship and shows a card with its name, type and distance

Sea Chart: the chart fits the screen at any size, so on a phone held sideways the key, zoom buttons and Ship are no longer pushed off the bottom and on a phone held upright the title wraps instead of being cut off
Sea Chart: naming an island no longer makes the chart jump
Sea Chart: the chart no longer gets stuck in a fallback font if it opens before the game's fonts finish loading
Sea Chart: on phones the Close and zoom buttons keep their size and the zoom buttons grey out at the closest and farthest zoom
Etheric Sea: Your Ship can no longer be boarded from past the Veil, which carried the player to the Iliac Bay without the crossing, while leaving it still returns them to where they boarded

Decorator: the furniture catalogue, the pieces in the room, the built-in pieces and the player's own things are laid out as picture tiles showing each piece's own 3D model, name, price and badges for what it does (holds things, gives light, crafting station), with a Pictures / List switch bringing the old lines back
Decorator: every tab, type, size and filter has its own icon, filters sit under named rows (Sort, Type, Size, Show only), and on phones they fold behind one Filters button that shows how many are set
Decorator: a placed piece's buttons are grouped by what they do (Arrange, Light and storage, Crafting station), with Remove standing alone marked as the costly one
Decorator: the placing bar is icon buttons with a Keys button that shows the controls only on request, and on a portrait phone the bar spans the full screen width
Shops: every shelf item shows its price before it is clicked, and a List / Pictures switch shows both sides as item tiles

Shops: the player's side is labelled "Your pack", the footer shows "To pay" (or "You get") and "Your gold" as separate figures, a magic-only counter is titled "Sell magic items" and Steal sits apart from the other buttons

Stores: the Stores page opens with a row of station tiles marked Here or Away, a station the player is away from stays folded until its tile is tapped, and smelting, other workings and patterns appear as cards instead of long lines
Stores: materials and items on the Stores page, the Notice Board's Market and Vendors and the Vendor page show the game's own item pictures
Shops: a button that cannot be used yet explains why when pressed instead of sitting greyed out with no reason, in the Reforge, Sigil Broker, shipyards and merchants
Shipyards: shipmaster cards show each ship's own 3D picture, and the Reforge, shipyard and naval-yard pages and a merchant's options each have their own icon
Decorator: panel previews (bank, decorator) no longer show the world behind their background
Decorator: on landscape phones the decorator's catalogue is no longer squeezed to a sliver
Shops: the shop header no longer squashes the shop's name on a phone
Weather: it rains about half as often, a woodland spring that used to be wet a third of the time now about one hour in six, the dry hours being the region's usual sun, cloud, grey deck and fog

Weather: rain comes in every strength, each front having its own: about a third are a light sprinkle from edge to middle, most a steady shower and only about a quarter build to a downpour at their heart, while walking into a front still starts light at its edge
Weather: thunderstorms are still downpours but come half as often

Quest Journal: the journal (the L key) has an Abandon button on every quest except the main story's, clicked twice to set the quest aside, which keeps everything it had and stops running until reclaimed from the pause menu's Quests tab under Abandoned
Quest Journal: the main story's quests show no Abandon in the journal, while bounties and revenant hunts keep their own Abandon as before
Mining: Prospector (Mining 50): surface veins show on the compass from 500 m (was 200) while dungeon veins stay at 200 m
Mining: Prospector: on the Overworld each nearby vein is marked on its own and named by its ore ("Silver Vein") instead of one "Mining x N" group
Mining: Prospector: gems still come a tenth more often
Mining: Deep Delver (Mining 50): dungeon veins yield double (was +50%)
Mining: Deep Delver: every vein in the dungeon shows on the compass wherever the player stands in it

Motherlodes: Motherlode Sense (Mining 100): the day's Motherlodes are marked on the map and the Overworld from the start of the day, each showing its ore and, until it rises, when it rises (such as "Tue 13:00", on the player's own clock)
Motherlodes: Motherlode Sense: warnings still come 30 minutes ahead

Mining: Stonebreaker is now Surveyor (Mining 100): the player's own word vouches for unwitnessed ground so surface veins there can be any of that land's ores, while a region's own ore (Mithril, Orichalcum and the rest) still needs witnesses
Mining: Surveyor: quarrying still yields Cut Stone directly, and a player who chose Stonebreaker is now a Surveyor
Mining: dungeon veins no longer sink halfway into the wall but sit on the floor at the wall's foot

Harbourmaster: cargo contracts send the player only to port towns on the sea, where they used to name tombs, farms, inns, temples, manors and ruins (most cargoes went to one) and region capitals far inland where no ship can reach
Harbourmaster: a harbourmaster's board stands only in a port town, never at a tomb's or a farm's shore
Harbourmaster: a cargo already held for such a place is cancelled with a notice ("Contract void - ... No ship can make port there.") and standing with the crown is unchanged
Gathering: felling a tree has the axe's swing and its bite into the trunk (a Clean Cut rings fuller), the tree groaning when it starts to give, its crash as it lands, and the logs gathered up
Gathering: mining has the pick striking rock, the ring of a strike on the glint, and rubble as a vein or boulder gives out
Gathering: herbs and the Basket have leaves rustling as the player kneels, the herb pulling free (or bruising), and the Basket's find
Gathering: skinning has the knife's strokes climbing along the line, a tear when it slips, and the pelt peeling free
Gathering: net fishing has the throw, the splash where the net lands, the water by the floats while waiting, the tug, the catch fighting as it is hauled, and the net coming in
Gathering: goods going into the bag, a clean finish and a new rank each have a chime
Gathering: an axe or pick blow sounds the moment the tool hits, not when the button is pressed, with its sound, weight and chunks landing together at any frame rate
Gathering: each gathering sound comes from where it happens: the tree, the vein, or where the net landed

Gathering: the tool stays in hand through the last swing, and the tree starts to fall or the vein crumbles as that last blow lands instead of when the button is pressed, without starting the next tree or vein cutting that blow short

Gathering: on the Enhanced skin each axe or pick blow dips the view and hands slightly as it lands, a little deeper for a Clean Cut or a strike on the glint and always lighter than a weapon technique's hit
Gathering: the blow's weight follows Technique camera motion (Settings > Accessibility > Motion) and never plays when the system asks for reduced motion
Mining: a vein or a Motherlode cracks as it is worked, and so does a boulder's loose stone, the cracks spreading out from its middle with each blow until it breaks

Mining: every blow knocks chunks of ore loose toward the player, landing on the ground where they fall (slopes included), lying a moment and sinking away, with the blow that breaks the vein shedding the most
Mining: if the player stops before the vein breaks the cracks close up again, and like the vein itself they are the player's alone

Gathering: other players see the player at work, every body type showing the tool swinging, class sprites also showing kneeling and throwing the net, Eye Of The Beholder sprites showing the throw, and Morrowind bodies crouching where the player kneels

Gathering: other players hear it too from where the player is working: each chop and strike as it lands, the herb pulled, the knife, the net thrown and landing, the water while it waits, the tug and the haul, with a blow taken back with Escape not heard
Gathering: the still paperdoll (shown while a sprite loads, or with other players' class sprites turned off) does not show the gathering, though it is still heard
Gathering: the Attack sounds switch for other players now covers their gathering sounds too
Gathering: the new sounds are part of Enhanced sounds on the Features screen, and with it off or on the Classic skin gathering plays Daggerfall's own sounds as before, now timed to the blows
Gathering: the veins, boulders, herbs and trees around the player no longer blink out for a frame when they finish gathering one or when the day turns

Tavern Cards: the Hold'em and Iliac Hand panels at tavern tables use the Enhanced Plus stone-and-brass look and the game's pixel font, matching every other window, and the classic skin gets the same look for these panels

DFO Grimoire: under the DFO Grimoire dress every mark on the card tables shows in the dress's own colours: the player's seat, whose turn it is, the winner, who holds each holding, the power that is ahead and the holding being aimed at

Iliac Hand: Iliac Hand's panel gets the fold button Hold'em already had, tucking the table's words away to watch the cards on the cloth, and both folds say what they do ("Collapse the panel" and "Expand the panel")
Iliac Hand: both panels fit on any phone screen, upright or sideways, and scroll inside it when the table is full
Iliac Hand: the turn is a track of six marks and the magicka a row of gems, with the magicka the staged plays will spend shown dimmed
Iliac Hand: the opponent's hand shows as card backs beside their deck count, with a mark once they have committed their turn

Iliac Hand: each holding sits under its own painted location card, their cards above and the player's below, with empty places for the room left on each side and each side's power next to its name, the side that is ahead lit, and cards never covering one another even on a phone
Iliac Hand: the player's hand sits in a tray painted as the cards themselves, with the picked card raised in brass and a card played face down shown veiled
Iliac Hand: online, the board appears once the game is dealt

Iliac Hand: a game ends with a banner ("Victory", "Defeat", "A draw" or "No contest"), a watcher's log line says how it ended, and the log keeps one line for each thing that happens with the newest always in view
Iliac Hand: when playing by keyboard the focus stays on the panel, so Space never makes the character jump up from the table in the middle of a game
Iliac Hand: the Cards page's switch, filters, deck list and deck name use the same look

DFO Grimoire: a chosen, hovered or keyboard-selected tile is marked again on every page that uses tiles, and buttons that cost something (Concede, Scuttle, Steal and the like) change when hovered or reached with the keyboard

Language: the new table's words and Hold'em's fold are translated into all 13 complete languages, and the magicka label uses Daggerfall Unity's own text, like the vitals bar, so it follows an installed Daggerfall Unity language pack

Project Legacy: the remains of the house's fallen appear where they fell, as a body with a line of light over it in dungeons and in the open, pressed like any body to take back their bones, heirloom and share of the purse, where nothing was drawn at all before and underground the remains only opened within a few paces of the exact spot

Project Legacy: the remains appear only in the dungeon the relative fell in, with spawned ruins, wilderness halls and the Arena's undercroft no longer showing another dungeon's remains, and a dungeon laid out at a different size (Smaller Dungeons) showing them only at the size it had when they fell

Project Legacy: remains no longer stay shut because of an enemy back in the street: being "in a fight" is judged where the player is (the dungeon or building they are in), not by monsters left outside, and a duel, the player's own arena bout or a hostile ship within reach counts as a fight too, which also applies to Play as, Pass the mantle and weddings
Project Legacy: putting the bones back into the remains no longer leaves the death quest stuck, as they lie there again and are still the player's to carry
Project Legacy: fixed a brief stutter when walking into a new area with Project Legacy on
Homes: when the servers are under heavy load the game waits longer between tries to load a town's homes instead of asking again every 10 seconds, which helps the servers recover sooner
Homes: loading a town's homes costs the servers half as many database requests

Accounts: when the servers are overloaded the game holds off on loading homes, yards, seats, traders, guild invitations, Marks and the save list and asks again later, waiting longer the longer the overload lasts, while the player's actions (buying, crafting, saving, claiming) still go through
Accounts: the servers also turn those requests away for a moment when overloaded, so they recover faster even before the player updates

Door Griefing: a door another player locked with a Lock spell is no longer locked for the player, and shop and inn doors in Daggerfall that trapped players inside (Lock Level 40+) open again, including copies a save had already kept
Houses: a door's label names the building that door opens, so the Issaqumbaa tavern is no longer labelled "Residence" or offered for sale
Houses: houses built on grassy hills (such as at some Temples of Kynareth) no longer float over the slope, as the hill now reaches under the whole house

Quests: when a party member's progress on a shared quest reveals a place on their map it appears on the player's too, and a copy that already says "Not on your map yet" is fixed by Settings > Repair active quests
Quests: The Lost Child: answering "No" by mistake no longer locks the quest, as clicking the child again asks again, including on a save already stuck after a "No"

Fatigue: running out of fatigue with enemies nearby no longer kills the player outright at full health, each time they hit empty losing a tenth of their health and seeing "You are too exhausted to fight - get clear and rest!"

Mace of Molag Bal: the Mace of Molag Bal works: draining a foe's strength raises the player's past 100 as described, spell points it drains count once even on two quick hits, and the bonus ends when the Mace is taken off

Crafting: crafted Superior and Masterwork pieces can roll the special lines loot can (focus, cast speed, potency and wellspring on jewelry and the weapon and armour equivalents), while pieces crafted before stay as they were
Court Writs: a writ's card tells how many of the material the player holds that it cannot take and why (only gathered or silver-bought materials fill writs), where it said "0 held" with no reason
Oblivion Gates: the Oblivion Gate boss's own mark and his host's paths no longer shade large areas of empty ground, so the ground markings in a boss AoE frame cost about a quarter less to draw
Arcane Specialisations: mastering two schools of magic allows choosing a specialisation, fifteen of them, one for every pair of schools, and the choice is permanent like a mastery
Arcane Specialisations: each specialisation has its own passive and a signature spell that the Mages Guild sells only to its own specialists and that does something extra when they cast it

Arcane Specialisations: the player is asked once when two schools are first mastered, told which specialisations are open if there is more than one, and chooses on the skill screen, and afterwards any time from the Specialisation card on the Master Skills page (enhanced) or the S row on the skill pages (classic)

Arcane Specialisations: the fifteen specialisations are Battlemage, Trickster, Riftwalker, Warden, Wardwright, Shadowcaster, Spellbreaker, Bloodmage, Elementalist, Seer, Lightbringer, Enchanter, Necromancer, Soulbinder and Hierophant, each pairing two schools with a passive and a signature spell (for example Battlemage, Alteration + Destruction, has Spellsteel and Aegis Bolt)

Arcane Specialisations: a signature spell is priced and trained by the specialisation's two schools, so a Necromancer's Siphon Life costs what their Restoration says, not their Destruction, even while mentoring a lower party
Arcane Specialisations: Chain Lightning and Rift Lance never arc onto allies, onto foes that have been calmed, or through walls
Arcane Specialisations: signature spells show their names in the player's language
Arcane Specialisations: specialisations work wherever Master Skills is on, and do nothing in duels and other refereed fights or against other players
Master Skills: online, every mastered school past 100 strengthens its own spells and not just their price, by 1% per effective point up to +40% at 200, the same rule as Destruction's damage
Master Skills: Restoration past 100 makes heals heal more
Master Skills: Alteration past 100 makes the Shield hold more
Master Skills: Illusion past 100 makes invisibility, chameleon and shadow last longer
Master Skills: Thaumaturgy past 100 makes Spell Reflection and Spell Resistance hold more often
Master Skills: Mysticism past 100 makes Silence, Dispel and Soul Trap take hold more often

Accounts: the heaviest read, the town seats list, no longer runs on the main database, which should bring back town seats, homes, the market and other online menus that were slow or failing under the account server's overload

Accounts: town homes, home rooms and decorations, gathering nodes, traders, Marks, guild invites, lineages, unions, cloud saves and the Arena board load from read copies of the account database instead of the one main database everyone was queued on, so menus should stop timing out and load much faster

Seats: town seats are worked out once a minute for the whole server instead of by every server process on every request, so the seats list, Watch claims, Levies, Tithes and sieges load faster and put far less strain on the database

Quests: a stuck quest can be restarted from its first step by pressing Restart twice in the pause window's Quests tab or in the chronicle (main-story steps included), picking fresh places and clearing its old items, links and topics
Quests: killing the player's own copy of a main-story foe (like the Dust of Restful Death's mummy) is no longer counted because a party member killed theirs
Quests: quest markers in small and medium buildings sit inside the building, and quest foes no longer stand on top of a hall's ceiling
Quests: when a quest's foe falls the player is told (HUD, chat and the classic line), and a quest box ignores presses for a moment so it is not clicked away by accident
Quests: an abandoned quest's item can be dropped from the pack and is handed back if the quest is reclaimed
Chat Window: the chat roster search finds every known player, not just the first page
Performance: clicking in the world no longer stutters
Overworld: a found dungeon shows as a dungeon on the Overworld grid
Compass: compass marks draw over the Grimoire frame
Text Font: the installed-font picker is a scrolling, filterable list
Account Recovery: new accounts get a set of 8 recovery codes instead of one, each code working once if the password is forgotten

Account Recovery: the Account section of the profile shows how many recovery codes are left, and Make new codes gives a fresh set on typing the password and one current code, after which the old codes stop working
Account Recovery: when codes are shown they can be copied or saved as a file (dfo-recovery-codes-<username>.txt)
Account Recovery: using a code spends only that code, and using the last one gives a fresh 8, so the player is never left with none
Account Recovery: someone who learns the password alone cannot replace the codes, so the codes can always take the account back
Account Recovery: the codes screen cannot be closed by accident (no Close, Escape or tap outside) until the player confirms they have written the codes down
Joinery: using a Joinery's workbench, or opening Esc > Stores afterwards, no longer crashes the game
Resting: beds in dormitory-style inn rooms (and ship bunks) offer Rest and Loiter again
Crew Spirits: once the crew has had the day's grog the shipwright shows their real spirits (such as "low") and says "Tomorrow" instead of claiming spirits are "as high as they go"

Magic Repair: the Repairs Objects enchantment repairs the player's gear again when they wear a Cast When Held or Item Deteriorates piece, which used to take every repair and undo it at once and is now repaired last

Town Watch: paying the watch's fine on the spot raises standing in that region by 5, up to the point where the watch stops recognising the player, where a paid fine only bought a day without stops so the watch kept charging the same fine
Loot Rarity: the life leech line reads "N% life leech on this weapon's own blows", and an off-hand weapon's leech applies only when fighting with that hand (switch with H)
Online Death: a death taken back holds, and the operator has a Realm revive run
Performance: arriving in a large city, or walking out of a building in one, no longer freezes the game for several seconds, worst in Firefox, thanks to ghandhikus

Horse: the horses' coats on the road's wagons are painted in under half the time, so the first seconds after entering the world stutter less and the frame rate settles sooner, with every coat looking exactly as before
Morrowind People: with Morrowind attached, Breton men wear three new heads and three new hairs (nine faces between them) on townspeople, NPCs and a Breton player alike
Morrowind People: each of the ten Breton portraits at character creation shows the face most like it, portrait 6 wearing the eyepatch
Morrowind People: if the new heads fail to load, Breton men show Morrowind's own Breton faces instead of appearing without a head

Morrowind People: eleven of Daggerfall's townspeople wear their own 3D outfits on the Morrowind body in their picture's colours (all four Redguard men, all four Nord men, two Breton men and the hooded Redguard woman), so up close a walker wears what their picture shows from afar
Morrowind People: hoods sit over the hair, and sleeves, hems and boots move with the body
Morrowind People: legs stay inside skirts, robes, kilts and the hooded dress as townspeople walk, and tunics no longer pinch in at the sides when they stand
Morrowind People: if an outfit fails to load the person is drawn without it and with no missing body parts, a woman wearing her modest shirt while Show Nudity is off
Morrowind People: townspeople without an outfit yet (two of the Breton men's pictures and every woman's but the hooded Redguard's) keep their varied wardrobe
Morrowind Body: the cape hangs from the chest alone and moves only with it as one stiff sheet, so walking, swinging the arms and sitting no longer bend it
Morrowind Body: leaning back swings the whole cape with the chest
Terrain: the Dragontail and Wrothgarian Mountains are taller and sharper, with pointed peaks up to 400 m over the ridges where they were 200 m and rounded, on ridges 40% taller
Terrain: the mountain woods around them keep their rounded hills

Billboard Look: a new setting, Billboard Look (Settings > Combat > With Morrowind data, off by default), makes Morrowind bodies and horses stand upright like the classic sprites so they look shorter with the camera above them, where off keeps their true height from every angle

Online Mode: loading an online character into the world takes about 3 seconds less, since the game asks the server for the family, character list, towns' homes and homes of arrival towns all at once while it reads the world, thanks to joaomdb3

Textures: ships (the galleon, the carrack and the large boat), wagons (the Wagon Cart, Open Wagon, Caravan and its room), the Stable, Wagon Yard and Joinery, the shipyard and lighthouse, the LeFay monument's stone and the tapestries, banners and rugs in towns use Daggerfall's own textures, read from the player's own Daggerfall files, the ships wearing the same textures as Come Sail Away's
Wagon: wagon paints are Daggerfall's colours, fabrics, woods, rugs, tiles and night sky, and every paint still applies

Textures: the caravan's windows and the stern windows of the galleon and the carrack are Daggerfall's leaded window and can be seen through between the leads, and the ships' stern windows no longer glow at night
Textures: the signboards STABLES, WAGONS, JOINERY, SHIPS and CREW are lettered on Daggerfall planks, and the Joinery's sign also carries Daggerfall's axe-and-sword shop sign
Lighthouses: the lighthouse beacon burns with Daggerfall's own brazier fire

Ships: the ships' stern windows glow at night again: by day the galleon's stern windows and the carrack's transom windows can still be seen through, and when the lanterns are lit the glass closes and glows warm, while the caravan's windows stay see-through day and night
Chat Channels: Trade is a channel to buy, sell and swap with players anywhere, with /trade (or /tr) saying a line there
Chat Channels: LFG is a channel to find a group or one more for yours, with /lfg saying a line there
