Running Hands: it works with every mod switched off, and a punch thrown mid-run shows at once
First-Person Arms: the Morrowind arms punch with both fists in turn, each with its own hand

First-Person Arms: a pair of weapons shows the left weapon in the left hand swinging with its own blows, now on the game's own skeletons too (which have no left weapon bone, so one is made by mirroring the right), with the arm not attacking dipping slightly at the shoulder
First-Person Arms: the Morrowind arms pump while the player runs empty-handed
Copied Items: when the realm finds the same item in two places it locks that item only, so the character keeps trading and nobody has to review it
Copied Items: a locked item stays with the player: it cannot be traded, sold, dropped or left where others can take it, while the wagon and the player's own storage still take it
Copied Items: the player is told which item was locked, once on each device
Copied Items: if the player was handed an item by someone whose game closed before it saved the hand-off, their copy is locked but no longer counts against them
Copied Items: every character frozen for copied items has been unfrozen, while the copied items themselves stay locked

Player Trade: the third time the realm's rules hold a character's trading it is frozen for a week and then reopens on its own, each time after that for a month, and strikes clear a month after the last one
Player Trade: the notice names the item and says when trading reopens
Copied Items: shop shelves no longer hand back an item the player already took, which used to create a copy by accident
Copied Items: another player can no longer plant a copy of the player's item on them through a body or a container
First-Person Arms: with two weapons in first person the left arm and its weapon are on screen, where only the right arm showed before
First-Person Arms: with two weapons in third person the arms swing against each other as the player walks or runs, where both swung the same way at once
Running Hands: the running fists stay low and pump with the stride, rising about a third of the way up the screen instead of half the screen like uppercuts
Running Hands: a running fist shows its back and knuckles like the fists at rest, where it showed its underside
Homes: a home's furnishings load faster, especially when the server is busy
Accounts: online features (homes, the notice board, mail, gathering, the market and the arena board) no longer take up to a minute to answer, or fail, as they had since the afternoon

Accounts: when the account service is overloaded the game backs off its background checks (mail, the notice board, the day's motherlodes) instead of asking again at once, so the service recovers instead of staying slow

Online Death: a party member's Resurrection saves a Bloodline character: while the death screen is up (up to two minutes) their Resurrection brings the player back with no death on the family tree, no Succession and no tombstone
Online Death: the death is held by the server, so closing the tab, reloading or logging in from another device no longer escapes it
Online Death: if the death is already settled, the caster is told "<name> has fallen for good" and keeps their magicka
Crime: anything stolen is marked stolen, including a robbed caravan's goods and the hold of a lawful ship boarded or sunk, so a merchant still buys it but never puts it back on the shelf

Crime: when the player is found guilty (jail, a fine or banishment) the guards take every stolen item they carry and say how many, while winning the case or leaving through the Thieves Guild keeps them
Crime: the player's own items put into someone else's cupboard and taken back are no longer marked stolen
Crime: paying a fine or doing a penance restores reputation with the people of the kingdom too, not only with the law

Town Watch: guards called into a building walk round through the doorway to reach the player, even between deep shelves or inside a closet, and attack when they get there, a locked door or a ladder keeping them out for only two seconds
Town Watch: guards and dungeon enemies standing next to the player turn to face them and attack, instead of standing still
Dungeons: a headstone the party has searched counts as searched for the whole party, the game says who searched it, and a stranger's search no longer locks it for the player
Dungeons: in tombs, coffins a stranger opened are the player's to search, and a coffin can be searched while standing right next to it
Dungeons: party members no longer vanish for a few seconds when the player goes through a tomb door
Arena Bouts: the arena waits for the server instead of briefly showing the player's offline rank and season, their title and wins never having been lost
Magic Repair: with a Repairs Objects enchantment worn, every worn piece of armour and clothing repairs 2% of itself per tick, the same as weapons, so a battered steel set is whole in about an hour
Stable: with horse care Off, the Stable page shows every horse the player owns and lets them ride any of them
Revenants: another player's Disintegrate no longer deletes the player's revenant outright but counts as a killing blow, and only the owner decides their revenant's fate
Market: market stalls look the way the pack draws them, with the keeper behind the counter and goods on the counter
Yard: stalls and boulders placed in the player's own yard are back where they were put, at the size they were placed
Shipyards: the shipyard's fleet page reads properly again
Professions: a pending perk change no longer blocks choosing perks when the player reaches a new rank
Guild Hall: the guild hall says what reputation still on its way means: it is already earned and arrives at most 15 a real day, and quests done the same day add to what is waiting, not to standing
Guilds: a member on probation is no longer expelled over reputation the guild still owes them, the probation being renewed instead

Player Trade: pieces of Ruhn's Regalia (and the raiding parties' sets) that were enchanted before enchanting them was closed no longer freeze the player's trading, and holds placed because of them are lifted
Gathering: the loot panel and its tooltip no longer cover skinning, or any other gathering minigame, while it plays
Instances: at a quest's dungeon whose shared version is laid smaller, the Public / Your instance prompt says the quest's business is in the player's instance only
Instances: Quest Repair in that shared dungeon tells the player where the quest's things are, instead of "Nothing was missing"
Dungeon Map: a dungeon's automap keeps the player's exploration of both the shared dungeon and their instance, and switching between them no longer wipes the map, its notes or its portals
Elite Gates: the Elite Breach is the tier above Dagon's Breach: a party of up to 8 goes down through the torn halls of the Battlespire under a 30-minute count
Elite Gates: a Weir Key used from the inventory outdoors, online and signed in opens a breach, the party at that moment becoming the breach's company and being called
Elite Gates: choosing Rehearse in the start window, or typing /breach rehearse, opens the day's free Rehearsal, the first circle of five halls, which pays nothing
Elite Gates: the breach rises for 5 minutes while the company gathers, then takes members for 5 more

Elite Gates: using a Weir Key opens a start window asking where to begin before any key is spent: Hall 1 or any Redoubt reached this season (or half the all-time best), deepest first, with a mark beside each party member showing whether they can make that start, the keys held, a warning if a tracked quest will run out inside, and a link to the Boards of the Spire
Elite Gates: before opening, up to three decrees, one from each family, can be taken on from the first hall as the Wager

Elite Gates: an arch of the gate's white marble and gold rises out of the ground in front of the player with a gold beacon 400 m tall, visible to other players nearby, burning open when the breach opens and sinking once the first hall wakes

Elite Gates: the Weir Key says why when it cannot open a breach here: indoors, in a duel or a siege, with enemies nearby, while travelling, in water or on a boat, inside a town, within 300 m of a Dagon's Breach or 150 m of another arch, while already holding a breach, while the road is shut, or without 8 m of clear ground for the arch

Elite Gates: wherever the party is in the Bay they hear a war horn and see a prompt with the time until the breach opens, answered with Enter (A on a gamepad) or the prompt's button, after which a portal opens at their feet, the opener steps through the arch itself and a late step through the arch still admits

Elite Gates: a key that fails to open comes back on its own the next time the player is online within a week, even if they reload, and a stake the Spire never settles is spent after two weeks with a letter in the mailbox saying why
Elite Gates: a call to another breach while the player stands in one no longer takes them out of theirs

Elite Gates: the breach is in the Timers row (its opening, then the hall and the count), gives a sight line ("You see an Elite Breach 140 metres to the North!") and marks the company's arch in gold on the map and the compass

Weir Keys: closing a Dagon's Breach can drop a Weir Key: the first close always gives one, after that the chance is 1 in 6 (1 in 4 with the rite broken), and after five misses in a row the next close is certain
Weir Keys: clearing an Abyss Dungeon's Hour drops a Weir Key 1 in 3
Weir Keys: everyone who has already closed a Dagon's Breach gets one key as a launch gift
Weir Keys: opening a breach spends a key, and the player must have closed a Dagon's Breach before they can open a keyed one

Elite Gates: there are four regions, deeper every circle: the Broken Galleries (circles 1-5), the Soul Cairn (6-10), the Shade Perilous (11-15) and the Havoc Wellhead (16 and deeper), each with its own enemies, lords, platforms and element

Elite Gates: a Brink opens the Soul Cairn, the Shade Perilous and the Wellhead, a long crossing through the Spire's broken passages ending in the new region's own set piece, the Brink into the Cairn always carrying its Sinking Stair
Elite Gates: each circle is five halls: a fight, a crossing, a trial, a second fight, then the lord's Court, with enemies tougher every circle

Elite Gates: entering a new region, the player falls past the Spire's broken underside of torn floors, hanging spires, broken galleries and upside-down columns lit by that region's glow, other steps being a quick fade and reduced motion a plain cut

Elite Gates: a hall is a way through the torn academy: corridors turn, rooms have more than one way out and the way climbs and falls between the arrival plate and the door, crossing over and under itself

Elite Gates: rooms include stair halls with a grand stair up to a gallery, towers with spiral stairs, two-level gallery halls, cloisters round a court, broken halls whose floor fell into the undercroft, and crossings where two ways pass at two heights

Elite Gates: short climbs on the main way are never more than two pitches in a row or longer than 9 m, sized so a character at Climbing 0 with no grip left can make them, each with a stair or ramp somewhere in the hall, while harder optional climbs lead off the way to caches and vantage points
Elite Gates: floors can stand over other floors, and blows, danger shapes, the legion and the lords all judge the floor the player is actually standing on, never the one above or below
Elite Gates: a fall that would skip the player ahead along the way casts them back, as the void does

Elite Gates: Yard halls are the Rift-Yard (close the rifts before the Sappers reopen them), the Wellspring (break the anchors, then the great rift), the Muster (cut down the standards), the Holdfast (hold the relic against the legion) and the Wellmouth (rifts that wander)

Elite Gates: Rampart halls are the Siege-Walk (fire vents erupt across the walkway, each warning a second before), the Falling Wall (crumbles behind the player), the Winch (two players work its winches), the Gauntlet (plate by plate) and the Forge Bridge (a belt drags the player back)
Elite Gates: stairs climb to the Rampart's caster pillars, the Wyrm's perches and the Council Rotunda's balconies, so every raised floor has its way up

Elite Gates: crossings are the Span's platforms and, from circle 3, the Deepway's chambers, with deeper spans carrying more passages and platforms growing in kind as the player goes down: drifting platforms hung on chains that lean as they swing, blinking platforms with a clock face and a gold outline where they will return, and crumbling platforms that crack, pour grit and click back into place
Elite Gates: walled Drops lead to a landing below with a doorway onward and a lamp on the far wall

Elite Gates: regions have their own crossings: Rails and Gusts in the Soul Cairn, swinging Pendulums that knock the player back to their last solid ground in the Shade Perilous, and fire Vents under wide platforms in the Wellhead

Elite Gates: islands carry waystones that light up gold where the player would be cast back, and a teammate standing on a crumbling platform that already fell for them stands on a faint gold outline instead of floating

Elite Gates: every crossing is proven crossable before it is seen: the Spire checks every jump's timing at the slowest build the game makes and lays the course again if a jump is ever unfair or the usual crossing takes far longer than the fastest

Elite Gates: if the player is still on the road when the company is pulled at the end of a crossing hall they pay 5% of their health for each quarter of the road not crossed, at most 20%, waived by reaching a new island in the last 15 seconds and never taking the last point of health
Elite Gates: after arriving late to two halls in a row, the next hall waits only 10 seconds instead of 30

Elite Gates: trials are the Proving Walk (a champion's duel) and the Athenaeum, where the Orrery's stones are turned to the true hours by pressing a stone's handle, every turn fraying it, a full fray lashing the whole company and Harriers harrying the player while they turn

Elite Gates: twists turn about one hall in four, trials included: a hidden vault, a Ghost, a Mimic, a Captive to free or a Squad of elites, a Deserter who closes rifts for a fast player, a travelling Sutler, a Scriptorium, and Dagon's Bargain, a vote to take on a decree for a Reliquary

Elite Gates: there are sixteen kinds of enemy: Harriers, Sappers, Ward-Bearers, Breakers, Casters, Divers and Lurkers, Binders that raise the dead, Wraiths, Shades and Thralls, and Dremora Lords and Kynvals, some Shielded and to be struck from behind

Elite Gates: the legion hunts: Harriers follow the company across the Spans and bite on landing, from the Shade Perilous Divers wait over the island ahead, enemies go through arches, up stairs and across bridges instead of through walls, Rampart Casters stay on their pillars, sleeping Lurker statues do not hold back the next wave, and blows land only from the fight floor with anyone off it for more than six seconds Hunted

Elite Gates: enemies stand on the ground they are actually on (a Court raised above the hall, a chamber past a Deepway's shaft, Harriers following down a course) and the player's blows reach them where they are

Elite Gates: every enemy blow is drawn on the floor before it lands as a disc, lane, cone, ring or the whole floor with safe havens marked in gold, giving time to step out of it, the Spire never stacking blows so nowhere is safe and a chained follow-up drawn dim until the first lands
Elite Gates: the company gathers on each hall's arrival plate and the hall wakes once everyone is there, the door then pulling the company to the next hall when stepped through
Elite Gates: the Count gives 30 minutes from the first hall, running during fights and pausing briefly between halls, and the breach tears shut if it runs out during a fight
Elite Gates: falling into the void is not death: the player is cast back to the last solid ground they stood on for a tenth of their health, never taking them below a quarter

Elite Gates: only two restoring potions a hall (Healing, Heal True and Purification) are allowed while every other potion and spell is free, the count refilling at each hall's wake and each Redoubt, surviving a reload and shown on the desktop HUD
Elite Gates: in the Spire the player cannot save, rest, open the map, use Mark or Recall, levitate, or bring companions

Elite Gates: ten torn-halls fragments each have their own danger; in the Galleries the Oblivion Caverns (curtains of fire burning 2 seconds in every 5, magma surges, falling basalt), the Fallen Stacks (shelves topple one after another) and the Broken Colonnade (column drums roll along the course)
Elite Gates: in the Soul Cairn the Ossuary has bone bridges that crumble and soul-wisps that drain anyone lingering, and the Mist Stair winds flights down into rising mist

Elite Gates: in the Shade Perilous the Gloam Thicket has black-glass branches that hold only while a moonbeam lies on them and the Eclipse Vault puts the moon out every 40 seconds so the player must stand in the walking moon-shafts

Elite Gates: in the Wellhead the Forge Gut has hammers falling where marked and conveyors, the Clan Pit has the Honour Horn calling one player into a ring with a Kynval, and the deep Caverns flood the low floor with a magma tide every minute

Elite Gates: cooling slag in the Forge Gut has two spouts taking turns pouring magma, crossed on the crust while it holds, its edge glowing white in the last second before it breaks and the spill's warning drawn on the slag itself

Elite Gates: a Deepway goes down through a shaft of its region's kind (such as the Hollow Trunk's moonlit branches or the Slag Chute), and standing on a ledge facing the drop tilts the third-person camera down and lifts it over the edge

Elite Gates: from circle 2 every Span forks at an island into the High Road (over the void, harder and shorter, with a cache of Reliquaries at its hardest point) or the Low Road (longer and safer with more foes and a Battlemage's niche that heals once and gives a Vestige shard), both ending at the same door, which waits for a companion still on the Low Road

Elite Gates: each region has a set piece: the Collapsing Tube (the cavern falls in behind the player), the Sinking Stair (each flight sinks), the Moon Path (walk with the moonbeams) and the Forge Line (ride the conveyors through the hammers, always leaving a way clear)
Elite Gates: the Molten Rim leaves gold causeways across its magma
Elite Gates: some Yards and Proving Walks stand in modelled chambers with a second floor up a stair, a chokepoint arch, surging channels, or an engine

Elite Gates: engines are used by looking at one and pressing it, or typing /breach use: the Sluice floods its channel for 6 seconds, the Shelf topples onto the legion once, the Drop-Hammer crushes them and can stun a lord, the Soul-Bell stuns Wraiths and Binders and the Moon-Mirror blinds the Divers and lights a branch to stand on, the others working once in 30 seconds with every strike marked first and hurting the player too if they stand in it

Elite Gates: the Honour Horn at the Clan Pit: if the player answers the Kynval alone the crowd throws every member a Reliquary, and if anyone else steps into the ring the crowd throws fire instead for the rest of the hall
Elite Gates: a faint gold seam in a wall marks an alcove that one blow breaks open, holding lumen, a Vestige shard or a page of the Annals

Elite Gates: the Annals of 3E 398 are thirty pages the Battlemages left behind, seventeen hidden in alcoves and thirteen given up by each lord at its first fall, read anywhere with /breach annals and kept on the account
Elite Gates: in the first Court the island Grath leaps from cracks and falls into the magma for 15 seconds, throwing a player who falls with it back onto an island that still stands
Elite Gates: in third person, walls, shelves, pillars and other rock between the camera and the character fade to a see-through dither instead of hiding them

Elite Gates: each Court has its own lord with phases, errands for the company and a fury that builds, every phase showing its card: Grath, the Spellmaster, the Armsmaster, the Cairn-Keeper, the Twin Lords, the Dusk-Warden, the Night-Stalker, the Colossus and the Wyrm, with a Valkynaz every fifth Court (Ilthys, Morvayn, Seyth, and Garoth from circle 20)

Elite Gates: Courts of two lords (Garoth beside the Last Armsmaster, the Twin Lords) are won when both fall, each lord keeping its own element, mirrors and decree, with the HUD showing a bar for each lord standing

Elite Gates: the lords have their own marks: Morvayn's chains let go of a fallen member and snap link by link, the Chain Snaps, a Soul Burst and the Cage Closes strike only the members they name, the Night-Stalker's true shadow glints 2 seconds before it rises, and burning bridges and falling floors can be dodged like any blow

Elite Gates: the Proving Walks have champions, the Kynreeve (Shield-Wall), the Kynmarcher (The Citadel) and the Markynaz (The Grand Duke's Decree, named on his arrival card and added to the circle's decrees instead of replacing them)
Elite Gates: lords and champions walk around walls instead of through them, through an arch's opening, up a stair and across Grath's bridges, and a Charge or Lunge stops at an arch's wall
Elite Gates: lords resize with the company: when a companion falls the lord loses that companion's share of health, and it comes back when they are recalled
Elite Gates: a Colossal lord looks as big as it is and can be struck at its true size, and the lord's health bar shows from the moment the lord wakes
Elite Gates: standing still, or with the game in a background tab, a lord's blow still lands on the player

Elite Gates: a death in the breach is a fall, not the end: a FALLEN card says whether a Redoubt can call the player back and how many Reliquaries were lost, the end theme plays, and the player becomes a witness who can ping the floor for the living

Elite Gates: the next Redoubt calls a fallen player back at full health once a breach at the cost of the newest Vestige, and a companion can carry their Memento from where they fell to a niche to bring them back sooner
Elite Gates: a second fall is final, and a witness can leave for good with /breach forsake (pressed twice)

Elite Gates: witnesses see more: dormant Lurkers, hidden alcoves and the next hall's twist, with pings shown as blue pillars with a chime, a row tapped to watch another player, and pings from the pad or touch
Elite Gates: if the whole company falls, the breach ends

Elite Gates: if the page reloads or the connection drops mid-breach the player is offered Return to the Spire while the breach still stands, even after the call has closed, coming back to the hall the company holds: at their last safe footing during a trial or on the arrival plate between trials
Elite Gates: returning from a new device or browser drops the player straight into the right hall, and if the Spire does not answer they are told and can try again
Elite Gates: joining or reloading in the middle of a fight shows everything at once: burning ground, Grath's fallen islands, the lord's phase and where every enemy is
Elite Gates: a breach that ended while the player was offline keeps their receipts, collected when they come back
Elite Gates: a server restart no longer loses a breach

Elite Gates: defeating a circle's lord takes its Redoubt: every member who pulled their weight has it recorded on their account, the fallen are called back, the company is healed and the Count gains time

Elite Gates: each member is offered three Vestiges at a Redoubt, picked with 1-3 or /breach pick N, lasting boons for the rest of the breach in families, every one working including those that strengthen their holder (Stoneskin, Second Wind, Searing Edge, Momentum, Bloodied Fury, Featherstep, Fleetfoot, Battlemage's Focus, Overcharge, Spellbane, Shieldweaver, Arcane Echo and Mender's Grace)

Elite Gates: Stoneskin's extra health is a true cushion, since the Spire's percentage hits count against health without it and its one-life count includes it, and a companion's Bastion, Steadfast Line, a Lifeline heal, Challenger's Oath and Immovable reduce the damage seen on the player's screen by exactly what the Spire's count granted, Immovable also stopping pushes while standing still on a fight floor
Elite Gates: a companion who has gone home or been left behind no longer strengthens the player's blows

Elite Gates: three Vestiges of one family resonate into a capstone: Rooted (immune to pushes), Spellweave (every fourth damage spell free), Rallying Cry (gives back a spent Second Wind when a hall's door opens), Bladestorm (the fifth melee blow strikes every foe around) and Deadeye (long arrows pierce the add behind the target)

Elite Gates: Accords take effect when their pair of holders stand within 10 m (Shield-Hymn, Hammer and Anvil, Ambush, Kindled Steel, Living Wall, War-Chorus), the offer card naming the Accord a pick would form with a companion, and Masteries are rarer
Elite Gates: spare shards buy extra picks and a Surplus buys a fourth card or a reroll

Elite Gates: at a Redoubt the company votes (1-3 or /breach vote N) on the next circle's decrees, each a hardship with a reward (gusts on every span, crumbling halls, raging lords, The Fraying and more), the Redoubt's beacon naming them and the next Court
Elite Gates: the company can ready up (Y or /breach vote yes) to end the rest early or vote for a respite to make it longer, which can be asked for again after each one
Elite Gates: the way home opens at the Court's heart (pressed twice or /breach home), or the player stays and the stair takes them down to the next circle

Elite Gates: along the way every hall pays lumen, caches hold shards, Spire Tonics and Cantrips (one-use spells such as Mending, Stillness and Long Step, cast with /breach cant N), and a Sutler sells them (/breach buy cant|tonic|shard)
Elite Gates: a Redoubt raises a beacon at the Court's heart, and each recall stands as a blue pillar
Elite Gates: when a Court's lord falls, the gate's chart shows each member's damage, share of the lord, blows, best hit, falls and healing

Elite Gates: at the end the recap shows depth, time, circles crossed and Vestiges, each member's share of the damage and what they healed, every fall, and the player's place on the boards ("The Descent, the Few: 14th"), surviving a reload and with a Close button
Elite Gates: each Redoubt pays once per arena week (Monday to Monday), and taken again in the same week it pays its gold only

Elite Gates: spoils are thrown from the Court's heart or go straight into the pack, decided when the claim is made: gold growing with each Redoubt, one Rare or Legendary piece (Legendary chance 20% at Redoubt 1, rising 3% a Redoubt to 65%), one to three more Magic-or-better pieces, the lord's named Legendary 1 in 8 (The Houndfang, The Examiner's Staff, The Last Lesson, Conquest, Tithe, Rivalry, Soulchain, Duskwing, Bloodmoon, Mirrorshard, The Engine's Heart, Wyrmbreath, The Clan-Breaker), the lord's own Iliac Hand card 1 in 5 (thirteen new aetheric cards found nowhere else), and sockets, a gem and the technique pass as a gate's spoils
Elite Gates: a Valkynaz's Redoubt (every fifth) rolls its spoils twice
Elite Gates: a circle's Reliquaries open once per account a week
Elite Gates: a Redoubt pays 20 Marks, inside the daily combat cap shared with gates, raids and serpents
Elite Gates: three members of one guild taking the same Redoubt pay 25 silver to the guild's treasury

Elite Gates: Deadlands Embers go into the pack at a Valkynaz's Redoubt (1, plus 1 more for every tenth Redoubt) and 1 for each Redoubt taken for the first time this season, to be spent at the Broker on insignia or the Panoply

Weir Keys: a Valkynaz's Redoubt drops a Weir Key 1 in 4, at most once a week, and elite foes in dungeons can drop one too: 1 in 60 in an Abyss Dungeon, 1 in 150 in an Elite Dungeon and 1 in 400 in a Regular Dungeon
Battlemage's Panoply: a new Aetheric Sigil Set of nine Mithril pieces (the Warhelm, both Pauldrons, the Cuirass, Gauntlets, Greaves, Boots, the Spire-Shield and the Spire-Saber)
Battlemage's Panoply: 2 pieces, Battlemage's Bearing, give +5 to +15 to every resistance and +10 to +30 magicka

Battlemage's Panoply: 4 pieces, Battlemage's Discipline: a spell cast arms the next weapon blow with its element for +20% to +50%, and weapon blows return 5% to 15% of the last spell's cost, an off-hand blow returning it only when it counts in full

Battlemage's Panoply: 6 pieces, Battlemage's Reprieve: a blow that takes the player under 20% (never a killing blow) raises a shield of 15% to 40% of their health for 6 seconds, half of it to party members within 8 m, recovering in 240 down to 120 seconds

Battlemage's Panoply: pieces drop from Redoubts at 1 in 12 at Redoubt 1, improving to 1 in 4 from Redoubt 16 and 1 in 3 at a Valkynaz's, a piece being guaranteed after 10 rolls without one, and the Broker sells one piece of the player's choice once a week for 20 Deadlands Embers

Battlemage's Panoply: in an Elite Breach the Reprieve and Shed Skin answer the Spire's blows, and death-saving powers (Unbroken, The Hour Turns, Shed Skin, the Reprieve, Divine Grace and the Ghost-King's Vigil) recover at the next Redoubt, not on a timer

Elite Gates: each lord has three feats: Unbroken (nobody fell in the Court), Swift (felled within 3 minutes) and its own signature (for example Unsinged, Grath felled with nobody caught by a burning bridge), and holding every feat of a region's lords earns Master of the Galleries, of the Cairn, of the Shade or of the Wellhead

Titles: the Elite Breach adds the titles Spirewalker (Redoubt 2), Beacon-Lighter (Redoubt 5), Kynbane (Redoubt 10), Battlemage of the Spire (Redoubt 15), Wellhead-Walker (Redoubt 20), the Unfallen, the Lone Beacon, Spire Champion and First of the Spire
Auras: the Elite Breach adds the auras Beaconlight (Redoubt 10), The Burning Stair (Redoubt 20) and Firstlight

Elite Gates: the boards (/breach board, the Boards button on the Timers window's Elite rows, or the start window) rank The Descent (how deep with one life from Hall 1, in three brackets), The Depths (the deepest hall this season from any start) and The Deepest Redoubts (the deepest of all time), and the Timers window has a row counting down to the end of the Spire's season

Elite Gates: the herald posts to the gate's Discord channel when a company takes every tenth Redoubt, sets a new top of the Descent, earns First of the Spire or the Lone Beacon, or a sealed region opens, and the first company to take Redoubt 10 gets a letter in the mailbox
Elite Gates: the count chip is gold above 10:00, white to 2:00 and red below, pulsing in the last 30 seconds, and shows a pause mark and why when the count is held

Elite Gates: each hall announces itself with an arrival card naming the hall, its objective and its twist, party rows show each member's numeral, health, falls and recall (an absent member shows an amber ring draining their 180 seconds), and every big moment has its sound and line
Elite Gates: short lines explain the Spire the first time each part is met, once per account, and /breach help lists every /breach word
Elite Gates: the panel, votes and Surplus work on touch and gamepad, the pad reaching every panel choice, and on touch screens a flick up jumps and the player runs at full speed on the spans
Elite Gates: Settings > Accessibility offers Danger colours (Standard, High contrast, Deutan-Protan, Tritan), Danger fill (50-100%) and Reduced motion
Elite Gates: the Spire's own words (cards, lines, the panel) are in English whatever language the player uses, for now

Elite Gates: the relay judges where the player really was when a blow landed, from their movement history on a clock corrected to theirs, so lag no longer counts against them, riding a moving platform counts as standing on it and the player's health in the Spire is the relay's count

Elite Gates: a feint is shown as a pulsing outline and fades out dashed when cut, a wind-up's sound plays only for a blow that will really land, and moving platforms run on the breach's corrected clock

Elite Gates: the next circle is built while resting at the Redoubt, off the main thread, so stepping down is a swap rather than a fresh load, and leaving the Spire by any route frees the circle's models and the region's textures

Elite Gates: a breach survives a server restart, picking up where it was with the downtime given back to the Count, the hall and every timer, waiting up to 3 minutes between halls for its company to return, a refused opening giving the key straight back, and an update that ends a breach early returning everyone's key and keeping every Redoubt taken
Elite Gates: jumps are more forgiving in the Spire: a jump pressed just before landing fires as the player lands, and a jump pressed just after stepping off an edge still leaps

Elite Gates: leaping and dashing techniques do not work on the crossings ("The Spire's spans are walked, not flown.") but work as usual on fight floors, and Slowfall and Avoid Death do not work in the Spire, where nothing is lost to the death penalty

Elite Gates: the Spire is rebuilt to look like the Fractured Battlespire, every hall standing in the ruin of the Imperial Battlemages' academy with columns, arches, statues, cornices and lamps around and under every floor in each region's own stone and forms

Elite Gates: each region has its own air and light, with ash and embers over the Deadlands' fire-sea in the Galleries, violet mist and soul-motes in the Soul Cairn, near-black dusk and silver moon-dust under a great moon in the Shade Perilous and smoke and sparks over the magma in the Wellhead, each with its own painted sky, the academy's torn wings drifting in the haze and the sealed Spire's underside overhead

Elite Gates: the lords are drawn as oversized sprites towering over the company, their hit area growing with them, and each region has its own stone (marble and gold leaf, slate violet and bone, black glass and moon-silver, basalt and iron)

Elite Gates: every platform edge has a thin steady gold line so the ground's end can be read even in fog or the dark, keeping its width in the Retro picture modes, and crossings tell more: Rails have a dashed track, Gusts blow visible streamers the way the wind will push, waystones are lit and the Mist Stair's mist is drawn rising

Elite Gates: danger shapes stay readable: within 30 m fog never fades a warning, safe havens are gold with a dark keyline and inward chevrons, the blow aimed at the player is drawn on top with a brighter rim while blows aimed at others are fainter during a trial, vents and fragment hazards show in the place's own white, and High contrast adds a double keyline and a hatch

Elite Gates: the Spire has its own score of fourteen songs for the halls, the Courts, the Valkynaz, a lord's wake, the Redoubt's hymn, the last two minutes of the Count and the end, with a motif for each region and lord, and the mix keeps danger audible: a blow aimed at the player plays a sound of its own, the music dips briefly under critical sounds and only the four nearest enemies of a kind call out their wind-ups
Elite Gates: when the way down opens a gold beam and a draining ring mark the door, which appears on the compass

Elite Gates: danger shapes lie on every floor they cover at that floor's height instead of floating or hiding under ledges, a "move!" arrow points the way out over safe ground, and tethers, burning pools, marks over companions' heads and the Eclipse each have their own clear look

Elite Gates: allies' spells are dimmed during trials so warnings stay readable, a Vestige aura is a thin blue ring, foes have a moonlit outline in the Shade Perilous, heavy blows shake the screen (reduced motion turns this off) and a Drop lands with a thud and dust

Elite Gates: each hall has its own echo (a cave, a stone room or open air) fading smoothly as the player walks into a passage, other players' sounds are a little quieter in a fight, Watchfire's early warning has its own sound, and event sounds briefly lower the music
Elite Gates: the Caverns' fire falls burn in Daggerfall's own fire, the camera no longer snaps back out of walls, a faded Spirebridge plank is no longer solid, and the Weir Key has its own icon
Elite Gates: moving platforms are drawn in far fewer draw calls, and those out of view are skipped

Arcane Essence: at an enchanting station Reforge with Essence no longer stacks its buttons on top of each other: each line of a piece has its own Reforge button in a list under the piece's name and price, and the name is readable again instead of wrapping one word per line

Crafting Stations: the profession stations' short notes ("Needs 2 Arcane Essence; your Stores hold 1.", "Needs 2 Steel Ingot.", the Stores-full note) span the row under the piece instead of being squeezed into a narrow column
Elite Gates: a stair rising above one of the Spire's chambers is always there, where a handful of halls lost it and left the way on unreachable
Elite Gates: a Gust only pushes players on its own crossing, never someone on a bridge or floor high above it

Loot Window: chests, corpses and the wagon can be filtered by name, item type, rarity and material, the rarity menu starting at Any Rarity and the material menu at Any Material, each listing only what that pile holds with a count, and a piece whose card does not show its metal, such as an unidentified magic item or an artifact, is not listed under one

Loot Window: Take all moves items from the list on screen into the pack from the top until the next item does not fit (emptying someone else's cupboard this way is still stealing), and Stash all does the same from the current pack page into the wagon, own storage or Materials Bag, the button sitting centred along the bottom edge of the item list and the pack page in use still starting on Weapons

Loot Window: looking at the player's own cupboard or chest, or at a stranger's cupboard already stocked today, lists what it holds the way a corpse or a pile does, with nothing taken until it is opened

Item Card: armour and weapons of Rare quality and above say their metal (Iron, Ebony and the rest) on the line under the name even before they are identified, a Legendary keeping its own name and so does one handed down as an heirloom

Titles: the $50 Hierophant Patreon tier grants its title and glyph in game, the rose "Hierophant" and the crown beside the name, appearing on the next sign-in for an already linked Patreon with no need to relink
Titles: WikiMaid is a new title, drawn amethyst into lilac into a bunny's blush
Titles: the WikiMaid glyph is a lilac bunny in a maid's lace headdress beside her name (and on the account card, the chat roster and the travel view)

Auras: Lilac Warren is a new aura of six lilac bunnies with cotton tails and little maid's headdresses hopping round the player's feet on a ring of lilac light, leaving fading paw-print tracks, with an occasional happy binky and sparkles of lilac, pink and white
Player Trade: carrying a Weir Key no longer flags the character for review or freezes their trading, and any freeze and strike a Weir Key caused is lifted automatically

Quests: The Possessed Child can turn out to be a scam (the child fakes, the Daedroth never appears and the child runs off with the relic), and a journal entry now records what happened and sends the player back to the tavern where the guardian was staying, translated into every fully supported language
Online Players: a player walking near the player no longer stands frozen for minutes and then jumps to where they really are
Online Players: a player who dies is laid down once, with no second body and second cry and no standing up for a moment on their own body
Online Players: coming into a place where someone has just died (in the Wild, for example) shows their body instead of showing them standing there alive
Online Players: a player who died in the Wild no longer stands up on their body for everyone when their connection blips
Online Players: stepping into a building and back out beside a body no longer lays a second body on top of it, and a party member's body no longer appears twice
Online Players: a player who has already got up is no longer knocked down again by an old message about their death
Online Players: when the player crosses into the next area, the area they left sees them change their armour or clothes

Online Mode: setting the computer's clock back no longer makes the player vanish from everyone's screen, leaves the game stuck on "reconnecting" or gets them refused with "token expired" when they enter a new place
Online Mode: entering a siege no longer has a rare chance of the server refusing the player for good
Live Chat: when another tab or window takes over the session, the World tab no longer keeps showing the old "Online" count
Online Mode: crossing into the next area while the server is updating no longer disconnects the player when the game looks for graves

Chat Safety: /block <name> hides everything a player says to the player (chat, invites, notes, letters, and trade, duel, wedding, card or journal requests), /unblock <name> undoes it and /blocked lists who is blocked
Chat Safety: a block is tied to the blocked player's account, so a new name or a new character does not get around it, and it follows the player to every device they sign in on
Chat Safety: clicking a player's name on any chat line offers Report or Block, a report sending the moderators that line and the lines before it

Chat Safety: /report <name> [reason]: <note> sends everything that player said in the player's chat with an optional note for the moderators, with reasons harassment, hate, sexual, threat, spam and other
Chat Safety: the game server signs every line it relays, so a report can only carry words that player really said and cannot be faked

Chat Safety: /rules shows the Code of Conduct, which everyone agrees to once before their first chat line, naming harassment, hate (covering race, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability and age, "jokes" included), sexual remarks, sharing personal details, spam and scams, while trash talk about the game is still fine

Chat Safety: breaking the rules leads to a mute, then longer mutes (30 minutes, a day, a week), then a ban, and a banned account is told its ban when it signs in and cannot sign in or recover until the ban ends
Chat Safety: moderators see every past mute and ban a player has had
Chat Safety: if three established players report someone within an hour, that player is muted for 30 minutes until a moderator looks

Chat Safety: guest accounts and accounts under 14 days old can post one public channel line every 4 seconds, while party, guild and local chat are not slowed and a line sent too soon goes back in the chat box

Chat Safety: for moderators, /cases lists open reports, /case <name> shows one (the lines, reasons, notes and the AI reviewer's view), /dismiss <name> closes it, /modhelp lists them, and /ban <name> [days|perm]: <reason> tells the banned player why, a moderator's mute or ban closing that player's open case

Dual Wielding: under Physical Combat And Armor Overhaul (on by default) a weapon in the left hand no longer rolls a shield block, as dual wielding gives up the shield's block as intended, where an iron off-hand weapon had been blocking like a leather shield and taking 5-8% off the damage a nimble character took, while shields block as before

First-Person Arms: dual wielding in first person puts the left-hand weapon as the exact mirror of the right, in the left fist the way the right weapon sits in the right, where it could stand well off depending on the Morrowind first-person skeleton, with third person unchanged

Dwarven Thunderlock: on the Morrowind body the Thunderlock is held like a rifle, the right hand on its pistol grip and the left supporting the forend, carried at rest at a low ready with the muzzle down and across toward the left foot, and coming up to a level ready stance while shooting, for a few seconds after and while foes are hurting the player, in third and first person, the Hourlock held the same way

Online Mode: the game refuses more enemies from any one player than an honest game can send and believes only as many elites, revenants and Greater Giants as honest play produces, where a modified client could stand huge hordes of enemies around nearby players and mark every one as elite

Player Trade: a crafted piece listed, auctioned or handed to a commission leaves the character's own pack (or home) on the realm at the moment it goes up, and one cancelled, expired or unsold comes back as the very piece that left, where a stale tab on a second device could list it while the live character still carried it

Online Mode: Renown, raid rewards, bounty and orc camps, the Watch, silver finds and profession XP count only for the realm character being played on this device, a character another device has taken up or one whose trading is frozen earning none until it is theirs again
Project Legacy: the family's record is checked against the family's own rules when it is saved to the realm
Player Trade: a crafted piece bought back from another player can be sold again even while the character who made it has its trading frozen

Martial Specialisations: mastering any two weapon skills (Long Blade, Short Blade, Axe, Blunt Weapon, Archery, Hand-to-Hand) allows choosing one of fifteen martial paths, such as the Blademaster, Ranger, Juggernaut, Assassin or Brawler, a permanent choice like a mastery
Martial Specialisations: each path has a passive of its own (for example the Vanguard's foes hit 10% lighter and the Woodsman gets fatigue back on every kill) and a signature technique

Martial Specialisations: the signature technique uses the Weapon Technique key whenever the player wields one of the path's two weapons and that weapon has no technique of its own, a path with Archery having a bow form and a melee form that share one cooldown, working with the loot ladder off, where a looted weapon's own technique sleeps and the signature takes the key

Martial Specialisations: techniques that give a timed effect (Rallying Cleave, Cyclone, Phantom Strike, Earthsplitter, Savage Whirl) start it as the player uses them, so every foe the sweep reaches gets it
Martial Specialisations: a player can hold an arcane path and a martial path at once if they master two schools and two weapons

Martial Specialisations: the choice is made on the skill screen, W on the classic sheet or the Martial Specialisation card under Master Skills on the enhanced skin, and the game also asks once the first time a path opens
Master Skills: online, a mastered Long Blade or Archery skill past 100 makes every blow land up to 40% harder at 200, where past 100 only raised to-hit, which is capped at 97%

Master Skills: online, a mastered Axe skill past 100 lands up to 80% harder against wounded foes (under half health) and Blunt Weapon up to 80% harder against fresh foes (half health or more), each landing up to 40% harder on every blow against the Oblivion Gate's court, the Elite Gates, the Remnant and the sea serpent, whose health the server keeps
Master Skills: online, a mastered Short Blade skill past 100 swings up to 40% faster, while Hand-to-Hand's damage already grew with the skill and still does
Fists: fists benefit from the player's bonuses: Firmament fist stars, sets and loot powers never applied to bare-handed blows and now do, while Werewolf claws are unchanged
Master Skills: every short blade swings like a dagger, where the Tanto, Shortsword and Wakizashi were swinging at long-blade speed

Firmament: every weapon family has two Firmament notables that raise its skill, and Axe and Blunt get a third; Blade Dancer, Iron Knuckles, Headsman and Bonebreaker keep every stat and gain the skill on top, and the Ritual's Battlemage's Focus is now Templar's Mace, a mace notable, with no star moved so shared build codes still load
Stats Card: opening the Stats page no longer changes the player's next blows, where it used to spend a set's Riposte or Battlemage's Discipline and nudge the rounding of damage bonuses
Martial Specialisations: choosing a specialisation (arcane or martial) says so in one line that fits the classic screen

Ship Hold: F4 (rebindable, "Cargo" under Come Sail Away) opens the hold of the ship the player is on, at the helm, on deck or in the cabin, and away from it opens the last ship they helmed or the first ship in their fleet with a hold, wherever it is moored or laid up

Ship Hold: the helm panel and each ship on the Fleet page have a Hold button, and the hold works as real storage in the Enhanced inventory where cargo can be put in as well as taken out, a laid-up ship's packed weight updating when the hold closes

Pirates: if pirates raid the player while they are ashore with their cabin ship and they beat them, the raid ends, the crews that kept spawning passively after the fight are gone and leftover raiders are removed from the street and the room, and the player cannot fast-travel away from a raid still going

Ramming: ramming a ship hard enough locks the two ships together for 20 seconds, the enemy lowering its sails and slowing to a crawl while its guns keep firing, and the player can board straight away without battering the enemy into surrender first, the whole enemy crew fighting them, with the target card showing "Fouled - E: board" while the ship is in reach

Shot Types: each battery can be loaded with round, grape, chain or heated shot, the broadsides sharing one load and the bow chasers and stern guns each having their own: grape kills crew and does little to the hull and loses force at long range, chain shreds sails and rigging, and heated shot often sets the hull on fire and a hit to the sails can set them burning

Shot Types: the load is changed with the mouse wheel while aiming, the helm's Shot button or the new Shot key (unbound by default, under Combat), switching unloads a ready battery and reloads it, each load has its own ball, muzzle flash, splash and hit, and pirates coming alongside to board load grape

Naval Combat: gun smoke drifts with the wind, a broadside leaving a bank of smoke that hangs over the fight and drifts downwind and smoke from a burning or damaged ship trailing away from it, and each cannonball lands with a tall spout of water scaled up with distance so far-off shots can be seen

Naval Combat: a ball passing close to the player's ship whistles, louder the closer it passes, and one landing right beside it throws water over the rail and rocks the deck, the side the shot came from (bow, stern, port or starboard) flashing on the helm plate with the hull bar showing how much was lost

Naval Combat: a ship that sinks while on fire may blow its powder magazine, every player seeing the same blast, air bubbles up where a ship goes under, and a badly damaged player's ship has smoke rising along the deck

Naval Combat: the target card shows the enemy's crew, the broadside's tally says how many crew went down so grapeshot can be seen working, and each battery shows how many seconds it has left to reload

Naval Combat: within 700 m of a hostile ship a journey runs at normal speed, where an avoided encounter could carry the player past a pirate at up to 60x speed with the pirate firing at that speed, and the Overworld view closes when a hostile ship is near and will not open or start a journey next to one
Naval Combat: online, sea combat near another player always runs in real time, so one player's fast travel or helm time acceleration can no longer speed up enemy ships fighting someone else

Flags: on the Fleet page Colours opens a flag designer with a shape (flag, swallowtail, pennant or burgee), a field colour with an optional division and second colour, a border and a device with its own colour, and Fly my guild's arms uses the guild's heraldry instead and updates when the guild changes it
Flags: the flag is real waving cloth at the masthead in place of the old pennant, sized to the hull and seen by every player

Ships at Sea: sea ships fly their own colours: navies use their kingdom's paint and royal ensign (Daggerfall's blue with the dagger, Wayrest's crimson with the rose, Sentinel's gold with the sun), merchant ships each belong to one of eight trading houses with the house's paint and mark (the Isles' teal past the Veil), pirates use one of six crews' dark paint and black flags (skulls, crossed blades, serpents, daggers or bats) with false colours painted as the merchant house until the black flag is raised, and legendary ships have their own colours

Ships at Sea: a ship that surrenders, sinks or is captured lowers its flag, every player sees the same ship in the same colours, cloth flags show on ships within 450 m (up to 24 at once) and further away ships fly the old pennant, fading their flag in and out with the ship

Ship Paint: on the Fleet page Paint lets the player choose a colour for each part of the ship (hull strakes, trim and gilding and sails on the Large Boat, Small Ship and Carrack, wood stain and sails on the Large Galley, wood stain on the Rowboat) from fourteen paints (Oxblood, Crimson, Tar black, Navy, Bay blue, Teal, Sea green, Forest green, Ochre, Gold leaf, White lead, Slate grey, Tyrian purple and Tan) or the original look, keeping the grain, seams and shading and the stern windows' night glow
Ship Paint: painting is free, works wherever the ship is and is seen by every player, and Remove paint puts the ship back to its original look

Ship Paint: ships with a cabin (Small Ship, Large Galley and Carrack) can also take a wood stain for the cabin in the Paint panel, applying to walls, floor, beams and built-in furniture the next time the player enters the cabin

Deck Fittings: on the Fleet page Deck opens a top-down plan of the deck where crates and chests are picked from a list and placed by clicking, selected, dragged, turned with Q and E, removed with Delete and kept with Save layout, up to 24 fittings, each sitting fully on the open deck and clear of the others
Deck Fittings: fittings stand on the deck in the world and rock with the ship, can be walked around and climbed on and are seen by every player, the plan opening once the deck is loaded

Ship Names: on the Fleet page Show name puts the ship's name on both sides of the bow on a dark wooden board with the name in gold in Daggerfall's own lettering, fitted to the hull's curve just below the rail and reading the right way from either side on every hull from the Rowboat to the Carrack, seen by every player, Hide name removing it, only a named ship able to show it, free and working wherever the ship is

Captain's Stars: a captain level (up to 30) is earned from sinking and capturing ships, beating off boarders, claiming prizes, finishing contracts, distance sailed, treasure charts, charting isles and selling goods at the exchange, each level after the first giving one point to spend in the Captain's Stars, a skill tree in the Firmament's style opened from the Captain page

Captain's Stars: the Master (left) improves seamanship (speed under sail and oars, turning, cargo, hull, repairs and better exchange prices) and the Commander (right) improves combat (reload speed, gun damage, accuracy, grapeshot, chain shot and heated shot, boarding, ram damage and how long a rammed ship stays locked)

Captain's Stars: keystones give a big bonus with a cost (for example Master of the Wind: +12% speed under sail, -12% under oars), stars apply to every ship the player owns, and removing or changing stars is free

Ship Refits: after the shipwright's three refit tiers each upgrade line has nine metal tiers (Steel, Silver, Elven, Dwarven, Mithril, Adamantium, Ebony, Orcish and Daedric), each needing a captain level from 3 for Steel up to 28 for Daedric

Ship Refits: each tier needs ingots of its metal or weapons and plate armour of that metal for the shipwright to melt down, only plain items being melted (never worn, locked or bound gear, quest items, artifacts, player-made, enchanted, conjured, Magic-or-better, Legendary or socketed items) with ingots used first, and the refit panel shows what each tier adds now and next, how many items it would melt and the level it needs
Ship Handling: with no enemies near, no ship chasing and no boarding or aiming going on, a ship's sails and oars give 15% more speed
Etheric Sea: every port isle in the Eltheric Ocean sells at least one ordinary trade good alongside its ether goods, Veilhaven selling spice, and the sea chart's isle card shows it

Ships: ship text no longer calls a ship "her" or "she" across the sea, the Fleet page, the shipyard, the crew hall, the Captain's Stars, the sea chart, the tutorials and the crew's chatter, now saying "the ship", "this ship" or "it", the Captain's Stars read as plain stats ("Gun damage", "Cargo capacity", "Guns reload 3% faster"), and the 13 translated languages were updated to match

Ship Refits: metal refits never melt valuable gear (worn, locked or bound, player-made, enchanted including the player's own enchantments, conjured with Create Item, Magic or better, Legendary or socketed), ingots go first with iron ingots before steel ones for an Iron requirement, and a refit payable with steel ingots and steel weapons together is no longer refused

Captain's Stars: accepting stars updates laid-up and packed ships too, so a ship summoned later no longer uses stars since removed, keystone costs (like Boarders Away's hull penalty or Merchant Prince's gun damage penalty) now apply in combat, taking a star mid-fight no longer reloads the guns, and the Quick Dial key asks before closing the stars window with unaccepted changes
Exchange: the exchange no longer lets the player buy a cheap good back at the price they sold it for when their trade stars are maxed

Naval Combat: other players see the same fight: a ship sinking on another player's screen plays its sinking sound, its powder magazine explodes on every screen alike, chain shot and grapeshot kill crew on ships another player controls, a rammed ship being boarded keeps its flag up on other players' screens and ramming a ship another player controls locks it for boarding on every screen

Naval Combat: the shot wheel steps once per scroll on a trackpad, the tally's crew count matches what the enemy actually loses, a hit on one of the player's moored ships no longer flashes the helm plate or shakes the camera, sailing up to an already sinking ship no longer replays its sinking or explosion, a ram that sinks a ship no longer tells the player to board it, and the hull bar is correct when taking the helm of a different ship
Ship Names: name boards no longer show on hidden players' boats or float in the room when indoors, and other players see a board shown or hidden right away
Deck Fittings: deck crates no longer disappear from the deck after the player has visited several houses
Ship Paint: another player's cabin shows its original look, not the player's own ship's stain

Ship Hold: taking cargo out of a packed ship's hold no longer counts its weight twice, putting a packed ship's parts in its own hold no longer loses the ship, a rowboat's plunder can be opened, F4 no longer opens a ship the player cannot otherwise reach, and the hold can be bound to a controller button
Ships: the Fleet page no longer says a hold or deck plan opened when it did not
Naval Combat: the aiming arcs stay visible in a crowded fight full of grapeshot and chain shot

Ships: there is no stutter the first time a named or painted ship comes into view, painted sea ships no longer slow rendering, and deck fittings, near-miss checks, the out-of-combat speed check and damaged-ship smoke are all faster

Revenant Gear: sworn revenants have ten gear slots (a weapon, a shield, a helm, two pauldrons, a cuirass, gauntlets, greaves, boots and a charm), opened by Gear on a companion's card on the Companions page (pause menu, Holdings) to give pieces from the pack, with Take back returning a piece, people, orcs and centaurs wearing weapons and armour and every kind able to wear a charm

Revenant Gear: a revenant's rank limits what it can bear: Rank I takes up to Silver and Magic pieces, Rank II Dwarven and Rare, Rank III Adamantium, Rank IV Orcish and Legendary and Rank V Daedric, and a piece it cannot wear says which rank it needs, the wearable pieces listed first and Show more listing the rest of the pack

Revenant Gear: a piece given replaces the one the revenant would have rolled for itself with its rarity bonuses applying, a shield needs a whole one-handed weapon given with it, given gear wears down in battle like the player's (the Gear sheet showing each piece's condition and a broken piece marked and not worn until taken back and repaired), and gear counts as the player's inventory, returned on release with a deserter keeping the more valuable half
Revenant Arts: one revenant in three is born with an art: Mending, Ward, War Cry, Siphon, Barrage or Nova

Revenant Arts: against the player from Rank II (with Enhanced AI), Mending, Ward and War Cry are channelled, shown by a coloured disc around the revenant's feet and broken by hitting or hurting it, while Siphon, Barrage and Nova are thrown at the player and marked on the ground like other telegraphed attacks, a paralysed revenant unable to use its art and a silenced one unable too except War Cry

Revenant Arts: for the player once sworn, at any rank, Mending heals them when they drop low, Ward shields them and War Cry raises their Strength as it goes into a fight, and Siphon, Barrage and Nova strike hostile foes it can see within 12 m and hit harder at a higher rank, the Revenants and Companions pages saying what each art does

Revenant Missions: Mission on a sworn revenant sends it to any of Tamriel's nine provinces to Plunder for loot, Forage for crafting materials or Sell-sword for gold, taking one to four days of the character's time depending on the province (online those days pass only while playing, a day abroad being about two hours of play), and the haul going straight into the purse, pack and Materials Bag on return

Revenant Missions: each province has its own danger and goods (Skyrim's orichalcum and pelts, Morrowind's ebony and Dwemer metal, Black Marsh's venom), the odds depend on the revenant's rank and gear against the province's danger and are shown before sending, a good trip bringing the whole haul and more loyalty, a hard trip bringing half and a hurt revenant needing rest, and a revenant never deserting while abroad
Revenant Missions: up to two revenants can be abroad at once, and Recall brings one back at once empty-handed, needing rest from the road, after the page asks

Elite Gates: the Athenaeum can be solved again: in most breaches the Orrery's stones could not be turned (the crosshair never named a stone, the count stayed at "Stones true: 0 of 6" and the hall's door never opened), and each stone now answers the crosshair just above its gold ring, looked at to turn it forward or back an hour

Guilds: becoming a vampire no longer shuts the player out of the Dark Brotherhood or the Thieves Guild (joinable only by invitation, never sent twice), as membership and rank carry over when they turn and stay if they are cured

Guilds: an existing vampire who lost the Brotherhood or the Thieves Guild gets it back, rank and all, the first time the game reads their guilds after the update, while every other guild works as before with a vampire starting fresh and mortal ranks waiting for a cure

Guild Hall: expelled from a guild, or turned away for standing, the player is told how to get back in: at the hall they see their standing, the standing it takes members at, how many quests bring them back there and how fast it recovers on its own, the classic look's refusal saying the same
Guilds: a guild's quest-giver can always be asked for work as a stranger, even after an expulsion, each quest done raising standing with that guild by 5

Standing: a standing below 0 also recovers a point every 7 days of the character's own time, resting and travelling counting and online time logged off too, quests and that recovery raising a standing at most 15 a day online with a chapter writ on a notice board adding 2 more
Guild Hall: if the guild also wants skills the player does not have yet it says which, and a hall shut for the Season says the guild's halls in other regions still have work
Standing: the Standing page shows the quest count under each guild, temple or knightly order that would turn the player away

Revenant Stars: every sworn revenant has its own star tree, built like the Firmament and the Captain's Stars, opened by Stars on a companion's card on the Companions page (pause menu, Holdings), the card showing its level and the stars it has to set ("Level 3 - 2 stars to set")

Revenant Stars: a revenant earns XP from fights won at the player's side (more for stronger foes) and from missions it comes home from (more for longer, more dangerous provinces, until level 10), up to level 20, getting one point per level after the first and one per rank past the first, so a Rank V revenant starts with 4 points and can reach 23, with a message when it has a star to set

Revenant Stars: three aspects surround the Oath: the Blade (health and damage, with keystones Deathless +25% health -10% damage and Bloodrage +20% damage -10% health), the Grave (its art, with stars making it up to 40% stronger and its cooldowns up to 25% shorter, Awakened Art teaching an artless revenant one of its kind's arts at 75% strength, and keystone Grave Pact +15% art strength -10% health) and the Road (missions and loyalty)

Revenant Stars: the Road gives better mission odds, more gold and materials (up to +40%, never more gear pieces), missions up to 15% shorter, smaller loyalty losses and shorter rests, with keystones Fortune's Road (+30% haul but a mission that goes badly brings back nothing) and Undying Vigil (rests 30% shorter, loyalty losses 20% smaller, missions 10% longer)

Revenant Stars: the tree uses the same window as the Captain's Stars: a click takes a star and the stars on the way to it, a right-click removes it, changes are pending until Accept, the QuickDial key asks before closing a tree with stars not yet accepted, and changing stars is free at any time except while the revenant is abroad on a mission
