Morrowind Body: the legs keep walking during an attack so the body no longer stops mid-stride and slides, and an attack that is interrupted or cut short by the next one flows into what comes next

Morrowind Body: a Morrowind Body Motion switch in Settings, under Combat > With Morrowind data, is on by default and turns the new motion off to go back to the original animation clips, with its text translated into every language the game ships

Loot Drops: below level 20, an orc's or a daedra's metal drop is often a mid-tier metal instead (Elven at low levels, rising through Dwarven, Mithril and Adamantium to Ebony), so Orcish and Daedric gear drops less often for brand-new characters; from level 20 the drops are as before
Shops: online, Orcish and Daedric pieces dropped by orcs and daedra, and bounty rewards, sell for the condition they were found in even after a repair, like all other loot
Loot Drops: in an online room, an orc's or a daedra's armour drop is the same for everyone in the room

Leveling: online, maximum health is never below what an average roll at every level would have given with the current Endurance, and raising Endurance later, including from the Firmament's stars, counts for every level already gained, with nobody losing health
Leveling: every level gives exactly 5 attribute points instead of 4 to 6
Leveling: levelling up online no longer changes current health

Skill Training: the Stats page shows how many uses each skill has toward its next point, says when it is ready (and, inside the 6 hours between skill checks, how long until a rest or journey raises it) and says why when it is held (at 100 unmastered, or the 95 lock)
Skill Training: a "Skills can be improved" notice stays on screen while a rest or a journey would raise a skill

Class Skill Swap: on the Growth tab one class skill that is not mastered can be changed for a skill outside the class, in the same group, for 100,000 gold, with level and skill values unchanged, the page warns if the new skill could never be mastered and an heir keeps the changed class
Master Skills: a class with only one weapon skill (or school of magic) can now reach a specialisation
Guild Vault: hovering a piece (or tapping its name) shows its full item card, base and modifiers included, and unidentified pieces keep their names hidden
Guild Vault: the vault can be filtered by name, pack page and rarity
Guild Stores: the put in / take out form is now above the list
Guild Stores: leaving Units empty moves all of an item, and a new Put in all button empties the player's Stores into the guild's

Jungle of Bantha: Hammerfell's south-eastern shore, from Lainlyn and Satakalaam east to Mournoth, is dense jungle, with giant trees closing overhead and taller ones breaking through, young trees and palms filling the light gaps and a floor carpeted in ferns, broad leaves and grass
Jungle of Bantha: a humid haze hangs under the canopy, thickest at dawn and in rain, and thins when climbing out of it
Features: a "Jungle of Bantha" switch under "The world" is on by default, and the jungle is always on when playing online

Weather: what falls depends on the air where the player stands (its climate, the season, the hour and the height), so cold peaks get snow, warm lowlands rain and sleet falls in between, and the jungle rains the year round while the Alik'r Desert almost never sees a flake; the enhanced look only, the classic look keeps Daggerfall's own weather
Snowfall: snow settles where it falls and melts as the air warms, so in a thaw white mountains stand over green valleys
Sky: a hard, smooth arc that could cut across the sky at dusk is gone

Crafting Stations: every station spells out its quality odds as percentages, with how they improve the further the player's rank is above the recipe's and what landing every strike in the glow band adds

Crafting Stations: each station says what its minigame asks for the bonus: the anvil's strikes, the plane along the grain, every stitch on the beat, the chisel on the marked line and the facet that catches the light
Crafting Stations: a Tailor's clothing, a Leatherworker's leather and the town Apothecary's bonus are each said in a sentence of their own

Passage Under Sail: friendly merchant and navy ships moored at a port's quays can carry the player: look at her hull and press Activate; she is never the player's own, so she is not in the Fleet, cannot be packed and is never the ship's cabin
Passage Under Sail: her captain lists every port the player knows, nearest first, with the direction it lies and the fare (Daggerfall's ship fare for the whole voyage)
Passage Under Sail: after picking a port and confirming, the player boards at her helm and the voyage is sailed across the Overworld rather than jumped, with nothing paid until she sets sail
Passage Under Sail: if the voyage stops (an enemy nearby, a fight, loading a save), her captain sails on by himself while the player stays aboard, keeping to the port paid for
Passage Under Sail: at the far port she lands the player, who walks the rest of the way in, and stepping off her anywhere ends the passage, with anything put in her hold coming back to the pack

Passage Under Sail: online, any player at the port can book a ship there, and once she has sailed she is gone from that berth for everyone for the rest of the day, with other players able to board and ride along
Salvage: the enhanced inventory has a Batch salvage button, where pieces are ticked one by one or selected in one go with All Magic, All Rare or All junk
Salvage: a batch sweep never picks a Legendary piece, which has to be chosen by hand
Salvage: pieces that cannot be salvaged (worn, locked, set with gems) are dimmed and say why
Salvage: one question confirms the whole batch, listing the pieces and the shards that will be gained, and Keep cancels and leaves the selection in place

Layered Gearing: on by default, a character on foot is drawn in the helmet, chest armor and leg armor actually worn (leather, chain or plate in iron, steel, mithril, adamantium, ebony, orcish or daedric), each character using its own body
Layered Gearing: the profile's Skin card opens on a Look toggle to choose Skins or Layered Gearing (WIP), and Skins still lets the On foot and Mounted skins be chosen
Layered Gearing: Layered Gearing lets the Female or Male body be chosen, and keeps the choice for the rest of the session when switching to Skins and back
Layered Gearing: a worn Casual or Formal Cloak adds its hood and cape in its dye, over any armor
Layered Gearing: on a horse the player is drawn in the Mounted skin, and as a werewolf or wereboar as the beast
Layered Gearing: other players see a player's Layered Gearing look only once the servers are updated, and see the skin until then
Quick Slots: a new Diamonds style of ten diamond-shaped slots joins Off, Diamond (slots 1-4) and Hotbar (the default, ten squares) in Settings > Features > Quick slots
Quick Slots: with the pack or spellbook open, pointing at an item or spell and pressing a slot key puts it on that slot, with every bar style
Language: the game's own text uses American spelling (armor, color, harbor, specialization, jeweler, catalog), while text quoted from Daggerfall, Daggerfall Unity and the mods keeps its own words
Language: instructions and messages are written as plain, complete sentences, with "experience" in place of "XP"
Glyphs: on the enhanced skin the 2 and the Z are redrawn so they can no longer be mistaken for each other
Overworld: a journey no longer drops to x1 while the land ahead is still loading, holding back only as much as needed and returning to full speed as soon as the land is built
Overworld: an enemy camp that has not noticed the player no longer keeps the Overworld view down and the journey at x1

Shops: online, mending a looted weapon or piece of armour oneself raises its sell price again, a merchant paying for the condition found plus a third of what own repair kits, Repairs Objects and the Varla Stone mended past that; a smith's repair still does not raise it, wear after finding still lowers it and offline prices are unchanged
Shops: an enchanted found piece sells at the Mages Guild for its found condition, not as if it were undamaged
Hired Traders: hired-trader patrons pay less for worn pieces, the same way shops do
Shops: tempering a found piece no longer lowers its sell price
Gear Wear: a worn book that is found no longer becomes undamaged when it stacks with, or splits from, another copy
Layered Gearing: with Layered Gearing on, every other player on foot is seen in the armor they wear, not only the player and those who chose it too
Layered Gearing: each player is drawn in the body they chose, or their character's own if they never chose one

Morrowind Body: two-handed weapons such as greatswords, warhammers and battle axes are carried low at the hip in both hands when running, held out in front of the hip with the blade trailing behind and the chest turning toward the weapon
Morrowind Body: running with a one-handed weapon and a shield no longer swings the shield up behind the head, the shield arm keeping Morrowind's own shield pose
Morrowind Body: the running stride is stiffer, with less knee bend and no heel kick behind, so the body rides higher and more upright
Running Hands: when running with empty hands or fists, each hand stays on its own side instead of crossing in front of the chest
Running Hands: in first person, the running fists come up in front of each shoulder instead of near the middle of the screen

Elite Gates: in the Gauntlet, killing a Caster silences its pillar, where only standing on the pillar's plate counted before and a group that killed every Caster was stuck with the door shut; runs already stuck get unstuck

Elite Gates: a lord no longer gets weaker when members of the company fall, since a fallen member's part of its health used to leave with them, so losing members in a Court makes the fight harder, never easier

Elite Gates: a lord is sized for the members who actually reached its hall, and a teammate still on the stairs or disconnected no longer makes it tougher for the rest, adding their part on arrival at the health the lord has left
Elite Gates: a lord still asleep in its ring when a member falls on the way to it wakes sized for the company still standing
Language: descriptions, tooltips, guides and messages across the game are rewritten in short, plain sentences, and codes and file names no longer show up on screen
Mods: mod settings say in a sentence or two what each setting does, and settings that do nothing in this game say "Has no effect"

Mods: the credits in the About pane say what each mod and library does for the player, naming every author, version and license, and two wrong credits are corrected (Roleplay & Realism's later parts and Eye of the Beholder's animations, footsteps and cart are already in the game)
King's Gambit: "Least stake" is now "Minimum stake"
Translation Packs: every language's translation is updated to the new wording
Elite Gates: the Elite Breach's windows use the Enhanced Plus style: the card offer, the run recap, the boards and the call tracker, while the classic skin keeps the original list window

Elite Gates: on Enhanced Plus a start window opens the breach, showing the Weir Keys, where to start, which of the company can start there and up to three decrees to wager, with Open the breach, Rehearse Halls 1-5, Boards and Cancel and the reason shown above the buttons if the breach cannot open
Elite Gates: when choosing cards, 1-6 chooses, Y readies and R takes a respite, spending a Surplus reads "draw new cards" and Enter closes the recap
Language: some of the reworded messages come from the game servers and show their new wording only after the servers are updated
Quests: every quest shows its objectives one at a time, with the journal and the quest tracker naming the step in progress and a herald line telling when one is finished

Quests: many quests, the guilds' and the great houses' best-known jobs among them, ask the player to choose how they end, such as sparing a wounded spriggan or finishing the job, or selling a lich's books to the Mages Guild or burning them as the temple asks, each ending paying and being remembered in its own way
Questlines: thirteen questlines run alongside the quests taken at guild halls and taverns, each opening with a letter or a courier when the player is ready for it

Questlines: The Dagon Cycle (The Burning Doors, The Covens' Hoard and The Weir Road) follows the trail of someone opening Dagon's Breaches on purpose through the Breaches, the Elite Dungeons and the Elite Breaches to the Valkynaz who guard them
Questlines: The Hour That Was Not has the priests of Akatosh feel a wound in time under the Bay and leads into the Abyss Dungeons
Questlines: The Old Coil follows Sentinel's sailors on what the World-Skin shed that still swims

Questlines: eight introductions (The Court Crafter, The Smith's Secrets, The Harbormaster's Word, The Merchant's Road, A Seat at the Table, The Herald's Call, The Bay's Troubles and Written in the Stars) each show one of the game's newer pursuits: crafting, gear, sailing, trade, the tavern tables, the Arena, the Bay's troubles and the Firmament

Questlines: a failed step comes back the next day so a questline never closes on the player, and a questline's page says if a step needs something switched on (Loot rarity, Naval Combat, The King's Gambit) or a registered account

Quests: quests that pay gear let the player choose one of three pieces made for the class (a weapon in one of the best skills, a piece of armor and a jewel, better the harder the quest), with each card showing damage or armor, hands and weight and Take asking to be pressed twice
Questlines: a questline's ending pays a named piece of its own, 22 in all
Quests: endings with guilds, temples and houses move the player's standing with them, and online a quest that ends unfinished still costs no standing

Questlines: online, the Dagon Cycle, the Hour and the Old Coil also pay titles held by the account (Doorwarden, Covenbane, Weirwalker, Witness of the Hour and Satakal's Witness) and the Covens' Hoard can pay a Weir Key once an account, only for what the service saw the player do: a breach closed, a Redoubt taken, an Hour broken, the Serpent slain

Quest Journal: the Quests window has a Questlines section showing every questline (running, waiting, locked or done), the step in progress and what opens the next one, plus each joined guild as a ladder of its quests by rank, and a reward waiting can be reached from the pause menu on either skin
Features: questlines are always on in the online world and offline are a Features switch that is on by default, while the classic logbook is unchanged

Dagon's Breach: some nights the Breach carries a portent, a third kind of mark beside the Warden's aspect and trials, always announced in the chat with his marks, on the map's card, on the marks card and in the Discord omen post, on about two breaches in five and never two in a row, and never on a Legion-Lord night
Dagon's Breach: the Vanguard portent puts the player on the Bridgehead, a platform out in the fire, with the Warden waiting in his court across it and not waking until his vanguard is broken
Dagon's Breach: the Sundering portent makes the Warden tear in two at the second phase

Dagon's Breach: the Captive portent chains a knight of the Covenant (one of 8, drawn by the night, such as Sir Evrard and Dame Lysandre) in the Pen, a platform east of the first court that a walkway rises to when the Warden wakes
Dagon's Breach: the Dire Breach portent is the Vanguard and the Sundering on the same night

Dagon's Breach: on a Vanguard night the first wave rises from the fire 6 seconds after the first fighter lands and each next wave comes when a quarter or fewer of the last still stand or after 30 seconds, and clearing the Bridgehead's 3 waves raises a walkway to the Muster, whose third wave brings the Markynaz, the Warden's lieutenant, who calls Imps out of the fire every 15 seconds and whose Imps crumble with him when he falls

Dagon's Breach: new foes are the Brute (a Daedroth that smashes the ground around it), the Caster (which keeps its distance and throws bolts of the Warden's element at the player's feet) and the Markynaz (a Daedra Lord whose Rend hits hard and wide)
Dagon's Breach: the Vanguard's waves are sized to how many fighters stand on the platform and the Warden has less health on a Vanguard night, so the night takes no longer than a plain one
Dagon's Breach: stalling too long (4 minutes) on a Vanguard night makes the Warden tire of waiting and start dropping meteors on the platforms (twice each if he is Echoing)
Dagon's Breach: the Warden's bar shows progress through the Vanguard, such as "The Vanguard - Bridgehead, wave 2 of 3"

Dagon's Breach: on a Sundering night Valkynaz Ruhn leaps to his court's heart and calls the Sundering (a disc 8 m wide to step out of), then tears himself in two: Ruhn's Blade, his body, and Ruhn's Flame, his aspect's fire made flesh (Ruhn's Rime, Storm or Venom under his other aspects)

Dagon's Breach: with 4 or more fighters the Blade bounds to the Burning Court and the Flame to the third court over the Rift Way, a new walkway, while with fewer both fight side by side in the Burning Court
Dagon's Breach: the Blade keeps the Warden's steel (Cleave, Ground Slam, Charge, Leap, Chains) and the Flame keeps his fire (Hellfire, Meteor, Flame Nova, Dagon's Brand)

Dagon's Breach: each half has its own health on its own track under the Warden's bar, kneels for 20 seconds when brought down and gets back up if the other half is not brought down before it rises, rising with as much health as the other half has left
Dagon's Breach: a half left with nobody in its court for 10 seconds starts to mend, shown as "Alone" on its track
Dagon's Breach: with both halves down together they rejoin in the first court (the Rejoining is a 9 m disc to keep off) and his last stand as Dagon's Champion is fought there

Dagon's Breach: the Warden has six new attacks, none used again for a while after it lands and none in the first seconds after he wakes, the first being Chains of the Warden, a burning chain to one fighter near him that drags anyone more than 16 m away to his feet for a Ground Slam
Dagon's Breach: Dagon's Brand puts rings under up to 3 fighters, and when it lands each ring bursts on everyone else near it
Dagon's Breach: Shared Torment puts a gold ring under one fighter and splits its blow between everyone standing in it, and only comes when 3 or more fighters stand before him
Dagon's Breach: Scything Wheel turns 2 blades around the Warden for 6 seconds
Dagon's Breach: the Burning Gaze hits and blinds anyone looking at the Warden when it lands
Dagon's Breach: the Unmaking burns half his court's wedges and then the other half
Dagon's Breach: when one of the new attacks is on a fighter, the order shows under the crosshair (such as "Chained! Run from him!" or "Look away!") with an arrow pointing the way out
Dagon's Breach: 2 to 4 gaolers rise as the first fighter steps into the Pen, by how many are fighting then, and do not move but pulse at anyone who comes near
Dagon's Breach: cutting all the gaolers down frees the knight, who stands in gold as the Covenant's ward over the court

Dagon's Breach: the next Dagon's Reckoning to land breaks on the ward and hits nobody, its crystals still shattering for the stun if broken, and a Reckoning broken before it lands leaves the ward waiting for the next one
Dagon's Breach: the Warden's bar shows "Gaolers: 3", then "The Covenant's ward" until it is used

Dagon's Breach: beating the Warden on a portent night adds one more piece of Magic or better to the spoils for each portent (one for the Vanguard, one for the Sundering and one for the Captive if the knight goes free, so a Dire Breach pays 2), and each such piece can be socketed, carry a technique or turn Exalted
Dagon's Breach: the Weir Key chance on a night whose portent pays (a Captive night only if the knight goes free) rises from one in six to one in four

Dagon's Breach: about one breach in five, with no warning, a Tithe-Imp bolts from the fire while the Warden is in his first or second phase, a large gold-burning Imp that runs from the nearest fighter a little slower than they can run and, if caught within 22 seconds, pays everyone who landed a blow a tithe of gold by level and a gem straight into the pack, or else dives back into the fire
Quest Marks: the destinations of the player's quests appear on the Overworld as gold diamonds, with the followed quest filled in and pinned to the screen edge showing its distance and time left
Overworld: clicking a quest mark starts a journey there
Overworld: dungeons are slightly smaller and stay the same size when zooming in and out
Overworld: while travelling, the Overworld tells what weather lies ahead and when it will be reached (such as "Rain ahead - 2.4 km, in 20 min")
Overworld: when standing still, the Overworld shows the next few hours' weather where the player is, and hovering a place shows its forecast
Travel Pathing: planned routes stay on the road from start to finish, including around corners, through towns on diagonal roads and up to a spot clicked near a road
Overworld: travel inside a town slows to x5 and follows the streets instead of running into buildings
Overworld: if the city gates are shut for the night, the journey stops and says why
Roaming Bands: other players being chased by bands can be seen from as far away as the bands themselves are drawn
Morrowind Body: weapons held while running no longer wag side to side with the shoulders, with dual-wielded daggers, one-handers, two-handers, staves and spears all staying steady

Dual Wielding: running with two weapons drawn is no longer stiff: the arms stay swept behind but pump with the stride and the elbows bend, instead of being locked straight back with the wrists twisted round
Morrowind Body: with a two-handed weapon (or a staff or spear held in both hands), the shoulders no longer twist with each step, so the weapon stays still in both hands
Morrowind Body: running is less stiff-legged, the knees bending and springing roughly halfway between the original run and the stiffer one from the last update
Lantern: a lantern hung at the waist on the Morrowind body is a belt-lantern size (about 30 cm) instead of full street-lantern size, matching the Eye of the Beholder sprite's lantern

Logging: every map square of the Jungle of Bantha stands 48 trees a day for Logging, four times the richest woods anywhere else, and every one can be felled: on ground that has not been vouched for yet, trees that would be Teak or Mahogany stand as Pine instead of standing nothing

Jungle of Bantha: the big trees stand about 16 m apart instead of every 12 m and young trees and palms stand at most one to a patch of ground, less than half as many trees, so the player can see and walk between them while their crowns still meet overhead

Jungle of Bantha: winding dirt trails cut through the jungle, meeting, crossing and looping, about one through every map square, with the ferns and grass keeping off them and the big trees standing back from them as they do from roads

Collision: trees, rocks, stumps, fallen logs, barrels, crates, statues and other solid props are solid on foot and on horseback, sliding the player around them, while grass, flowers, ferns and bushes can still be walked through, and a player who ends up inside one can walk straight out

Gathering Nodes: herb patches, veins, boulders, fishing schools, dungeon veins and trees have a crisp outline in their profession's colour that follows the node itself, fading in on approach, fading with distance and fog and hidden by anything in front, while a skinnable body drawn as a 3D character keeps the old glow
Jungle of Bantha: the jungle floor carries as much grass as meadows elsewhere, growing between the same ferns and flowers, which stay at the amount they were thinned to
Name Filter: the filter refuses names containing "prostitute" or "strangler", even run together with another word, and in chat, letters and notes these words are starred out

Quests: the questlines' givers (Ysolde Marnhel, Prior Anselm Vey, Hamid al-Rasheen and Corvane Tull) carry their own names on the nameplate, in the talk window and under the Info cursor, instead of a random name that differed from the one in the quest's letters, journal and guide, and every quest's people now answer to the name their quest uses

Weir Keys: Weir Keys stay in the pack and can no longer be stowed in the wagon or in storage, keys stowed earlier are cleared on load, and the account's real key count is unchanged because the extra keys that turned to rust on use were never real

Enchanting: the item maker takes each side effect's setting once, so a drawback such as User Takes Damage in holy places can no longer be stacked for extra points and an effect with every setting taken leaves the list, with items enchanted before keeping their enchantments

Wrothgarian Zone: a companion's pack is at stake with the player's there, so a death drops what the crew hand or sworn revenant carries, companions cannot be sent away from inside the zone and one knocked out there leaves its pack with the player

Spells: Disintegrate works on online bosses (the Oblivion Gate Warden, his crystals and host, the Abyss Dungeon's Remnant, Elite Breach foes and arena opponents), landing the biggest blow the fight allows instead of nothing, and spell damage numbers on these bosses show what can actually land

Spells: damage-over-time spells keep burning on those online bosses (not arena opponents) and the sea serpent instead of stopping after their first hit, and recasting refreshes the effect rather than stacking it
Spells: Chain Lightning, Earthshaker and Dragonfire show their own damage numbers, tagged with the power's name
Elite Gates: the Gauntlet's caster plates glow gold on their pillars and dim once that caster is silenced, and the objective names both ways to silence a caster: hold its plate or slay it
Duels: in a duel the health bar shows the duel vitality and drops when the opponent hits, going back to real health when the duel ends, while duels still never touch real health
Collision: furniture in a player's home or yard, and a mountain, camp or town that loads in around the player, no longer trap them: they appear, the player walks out and they turn solid once clear

Dungeons: dungeon lifts and moving floors no longer trap the player or push them out of the map, a lift that meets the head waits until the player steps clear, a lowering floor stops above them and a player who falls out of a dungeon is returned to its entrance
Town Map: Find me takes the player to where they are standing, zooming to the street and marking them with the red cross, instead of jumping to the edge of town
Dungeon Map: Find me on the dungeon map also brings the player back to their own floor

Guild Refusal: at a guild's Buy Spells counter, a purchase the shop refuses says why (no spellbook, or not enough gold) instead of doing nothing, the message goes away with a click and Leave works on the next press
Guild Refusal: a guild or coven whose quest the player has not finished says so and names that quest, instead of "That service is not available yet."

Invisibility: worn items that make the player invisible, blending or a shade no longer stay switched off after a blow lands, the effect coming back on its own within six game hours while the item is still worn
Status Box: catching a disease shows an "Unwell" tile on the Enhanced HUD and "You feel unwell." in the Status box while it incubates, the disease's name appearing once its symptoms begin

Enchanting: the Enchanting Station lists crafted pieces too small to give Arcane Essence, greaves and pauldrons among them, grayed out with the reason: a piece needs 100 enchantment points for one Essence
Revenants: revenants no longer take the player's horse, cart, deeds or spellbook, and anything one took before comes back to the pack on the next load with a message

Heirlooms: an heir can reach the remains of an ancestor who died inside another player's instance: where the shared dungeon is laid smaller, its door offers an instance of the heir's own and the remains lie where they fell

Letters of Credit: characters left with negative gold by the old large-sale bug can be repaired by staff, resetting the gold, returning what they were owed as a letter of credit and lifting the trading freeze the bad sale caused
Server: gathering, the Notice Board's writs and traders, town yards, the guild chapters and the arena board ask far less of the account database, so they answer quickly in the evening rush
Server: when the account service is slow, the game waits a moment before asking for display data again instead of asking harder, and gathering, crafting, trading and saving are never held back

Abyss Dungeons: a new Abyss Dungeon always rises by a town, going to the busiest region on land or one of the Bay's great cities when players are crowded at sea, where it had stopped appearing when most players online were at sea
Abyss Dungeons: an Abyss Dungeon that already rose at sea shows up by one of the Bay's great cities

HUD: two tiles beside the Renown bar: Skills ready counts the skills a rest or a journey would raise, and Firmament stars counts the stars and craft points not yet placed and opens the Firmament page when clicked, both movable with Alt+U, and the level strip no longer shows the "skills ready" message
HUD: hovering any buff, debuff, need or disease tile shows what it does in the same card the inventory uses
Level-Up Notification: under DFO Grimoire the level-up notes are written in full, readable ink
Inventory: a Lantern slot after the Crystals holds a lantern that hangs at the belt, is lit while it hangs and goes out when taken off
Monster Volume: a Monster Volume setting (0-100%) under Audio controls monster calls, attack sounds and pain cries
Monster Volume: monsters call 60% less often, while the city watch and companions are unchanged

Quests: clicking an NPC that a quest is waiting on shows the quest's message and reward right away, with the talk window, guild or shop opening after them instead of the quest words appearing only after Exit
Growth Tab: the window no longer changes size when switching pages, and the page list always sits on the left with a short description under each entry
Growth Tab: the Level page opens on a card showing the level
Growth Tab: mastery bars are thin red bars, the same height as the yellow ones
World Map: a Players filter (Shown / Hidden) shares its setting with the Overworld's Travellers switch
Hoods: the female hooded armour no longer floats over the shoulders
Weapons: the mace head is no longer pale and black
Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: Kamer & Kab's Daggerfall Enemy Expansion 1.3.4 is in the Mods pane and on by default, and online the room's setting applies to everyone in it

Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: the mod's fifty new enemies are registered with their art, its changes to sixteen classic monsters and two classic classes apply while it is on, and quests can name the new enemies

Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: the new enemies animate and stand at the size the mod gives them, with glowing parts glowing and spirits drawn see-through in dungeons, towns and the Overworld's bands, female riders and Dark Slayers fall as their own female corpses and the Hell Hound's corpse burns outside dungeons too

Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: the new enemies turn up in every dungeon type, the water and each climate's towns by night, wilderness by day and wilderness by night using the mod's encounter tables, with laboratories picking one of two tables each, the same one every visit and for every player, and arriving in a town by fast travel or a load picking that climate's town-night table

Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: the new enemies cast their own spells, the mod's four new spells joining the spell list hidden from shops, each spellcaster casting its own book: King Lysandus his Bolt of Vengeance, the spellcasting classes by their level

Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: the new enemies' attacks carry effects: the Blood Spider's bite leeches blood, the Gloom Wraith's touch silences, the Fire Daemon's touch burns, the Will-o'-wisp's touch wracks, the lizard men paralyse like a spider, the bat and the ghouls carry disease and the nymph tires

Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: blunt weapons do half damage to the Skeletal Soldier and silver does double, as against the Skeletal Warrior, with Barbarians no longer taking that rule while the mod is on, and each new enemy has its own kind (beast, humanoid, undead, daedra) for racial bonuses, Detect, Dispel and Pacify and its own language

Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: the Troll gets back up ten seconds after it falls, unless a spell's missile burns the body to ash first, fire being its weakness while blades and arrows do nothing to the body, which cannot be searched, a Troll still down on a save keeps its time and a burnt one stays burnt, the mod's "Disable Troll Respawn" setting keeps them down and online every player sees the same body rise or burn

Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: with Morrowind attached, the new enemies stand in Morrowind's bodies where Morrowind has the same creature, the lizard men stand as Argonians and the new classes as people, while the riders, the flyers and the creatures Morrowind lacks keep their Daggerfall sprites
Roleplay & Realism: with Roleplay & Realism: Items' realistic enemy equipment on, Daggerfall Enemy Expansion kits every class enemy, the classic classes included

Roleplay & Realism: the new classes are armed as the class they are drawn from: a Knight Rider fights as a Knight, a Druid as a Mage and a Bounty Hunter as an Assassin, with the Assassin's chance of a poisoned blade
Roleplay & Realism: class enemies wear their second weapon

Roleplay & Realism: armour follows what each class may wear, so with the new armour on a class that may not wear plate sometimes wears the chain or leather set instead, a Monk wears about half the armour it did and Rangers and Burglars wear their classic pieces rather than chain or leather
Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: in There's a Hole in the Bottom of the Ocean's abyss, the new classes are treated as monsters, as that mod's own code does
Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: the vampires, the ancient vampires, the frost and fire daedra and the fire atronach no longer cast shadows, sprite or Morrowind body, as in Daggerfall Unity

Roleplay & Realism: with realistic enemy equipment, an enemy no longer holds a two-handed weapon and a shield at once, and an orc's poisoned blade is rolled before its gear turns orcish, as in Daggerfall Unity
Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: the mod's pictures leave memory once drawn
Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: the new enemies' names are translated into every language the game offers, where before they showed in English everywhere, as in Daggerfall Unity
Meaner Monsters: with both mods on (the default, and always online), Meaner Monsters plays as MUDEX, the version its author Ralzar made for Daggerfall Enemy Expansion
Meaner Monsters: MUDEX sets the health, damage, level and armour of 35 monsters, classic and new, with the Grizzly Bear hitting for 1-20 with 50-100 health and the Goblin for 4-15

Meaner Monsters: every dungeon type gets themed encounter tables that do not scale with the player's level, beside its usual one, such as a lich's, a vampire's, a mummy's, a necromancer's or a haunted crypt

Enhanced Sounds: the game no longer distorts when many loud sounds play at once: a limiter sits on the final output, so the Legion-Lord's heavy blows, his roars and the gate music cannot push the mix past full volume, and everyday sound is unchanged
Oblivion Gates: Hellfire, Meteor, Brand and Torment play at most two copies of their sound instead of one per targeted player, where a group's third-phase Hellfire played ten copies at once
Oblivion Gates: inside the gate, other players' sounds play 4 dB quieter, as they already do in the Elite Gates Spire, so the boss's warnings stand out
Oblivion Gates: the gate fight's spark, meteor, crystal and portal effects are prepared on arrival in the court instead of the first time each appears mid-fight
Oblivion Gates: the monsters a gate can field are loaded on arrival instead of when the first wave rises or the boss splits in two
Blood: blood splashes no longer redo their image work on every hit
Shadows: with Enhanced Lighting shadows on, the brief flashes of the boss's landings, his fall and the Wrath no longer cast shadows, so they no longer force shadow redraws

Titles: Severide, the first ever to take Redoubt 10 of the Battlespire, alone, in 1:17:40, holds the First of the Spire title and its aura Firstlight, equipped from the profile, and a letter from the Developers waits in the mailbox

Auras: Firstlight is a one-of-a-kind aura worn only by the first company to take Redoubt 10, with a dial of the ten Redoubts lighting round the wearer's feet one after another, ten spires of dawn-light rising as each is taken and, when the tenth falls, a sunburst across the ground and a shaft of first light rising past the head

Titles: the First of the Spire title and its aura Firstlight go to Serveride (seen in the world as Severide), the first to take Redoubt 10, where the last update had named the wrong account so nobody received them

Gathering Nodes: herbs, veins, boulders, trees and fishing schools no longer wear a coloured outline and catch the light instead, with small star-shaped glints flashing on the node and fading and, from a distance, a soft sheen passing over it now and then, in warm daylight with a hint of the profession's colour
Gathering Nodes: the node being worked goes quiet, with no glints and no sheen while picking, mining, chopping or skinning it, and no sheen crosses any node up close
Gathering Nodes: glints stay on the spot of the plant, vein or tree they belong to as the player walks instead of hopping about
Gathering Nodes: walls and rocks in front of a node hide its glint, and fog and the sea's murk fade it as they fade the node
Gathering Nodes: with reduced motion turned on in the system, the glints hold still and no sheen crosses

Gathering Nodes: the glints follow the light where the node stands, bright in daylight and dim at night, underground and in a storm but never so dim the node cannot be found, with a node beside a mine lamp catching its light, and the passing sheen going out at night, in a storm and in an unlit mine
Gathering Nodes: gathering nodes behind the player no longer cost a full-screen pass each frame
Witches' Festival: the first live event runs from 20 October to 7 November

Witches' Festival: killing foes, gathering, crafting, fishing, winning tavern games, finishing quests and bounties, sailing, the endgame and holding a fallen star can earn Soul Cakes, which go straight into the pack, the dead and the summoned giving them more often, and a linked account and being online are needed to keep them
Witches' Festival: every Soul Cake find is doubled on All Hallows' Eve, 31 October, and on the in-game 13th of Frostfall and 3rd of Hearthfire, when the dead walk (about an hour of real time each)

Witches' Festival: a Glenmoril witch outside the taverns trades Soul Cakes for The Wyrd's Raiment, a nine-piece Aetheric set of eight leather pieces, so casters can wear it, and the Witchmoon Athame, with set bonuses Wyrd-Sight, Tallow-Ward and Soul Harvest
Witches' Festival: the witch trades Soul Cakes for the Witchwarden title
Witches' Festival: the witch trades Soul Cakes for Witchfire, an aura of green fire and tallow candles
Witches' Festival: the witch trades Soul Cakes for profile icons, a new kind of cosmetic worn in the portrait instead of the face and seen by other players, three to buy and one to earn
Witches' Festival: the witch trades Soul Cakes for six festival cards for the Iliac Hand, including the legendary King Lysandus' Spectre

Witches' Festival: every town is decorated in its own region's style: turnip lanterns and straw effigies in High Rock, candles and bowls of fire in Hammerfell, bonfires and horned skulls in the mountains, ward-staves in the fens and bones in the Haunted Woodlands
Hearth Offerings: a Hearth Offering can be set out at the door of a home and filled with Soul Cakes
Hearth Offerings: other players can take one cake from each offering per day
Hearth Offerings: an offering can be taken back in at any time, even after the festival, returning the bowl and every cake still in it
Hearth Offerings: when other players have taken 25 cakes from a player's offerings, the player earns the Hearthkeeper title
Hearth Offerings: taking 10 cakes from other players' offerings earns the Soul Cake icon
Starfall: every real hour is a night, and each night one of the Bay's twelve covens pulls three stars down into the wilds of its region, each near a different town
Starfall: a new star burns in the sky for a minute and a half before it falls, chat names the town it is falling toward, and the map, the compass and the Timers window point to it
Starfall: a landed star is held: the coven comes in four waves, then their master, and what they summon goes for the star itself, the coven taking it if its light runs out
Starfall: the master calls a circle twice, and while any of the circle stands the master takes only a quarter of every blow
Starfall: an unheld star is lost 15 minutes after it falls
Starfall: on the 13th of Frostfall the night's last star is the Heart-Star, whose master's circle is twice the size and whose rewards are twice as large
Starfall: a held star gives Renown, 30 silver, gold, 1 to 3 pieces of Starfall Glass, a magic item or better and Soul Cakes, and the account card counts Stars held
Starfall: Starfall Glass is pale glass that still holds some of the star's light, stacks, and is paid well for by any merchant
Starfall: one star in four also gives a piece of the Starspun Weave, Mephala's nine-piece set, and the Heart-Star always gives one

Starfall: the Starspun Weave's set bonuses are Spinner's Thread (2 pieces: poison resistance and Agility), Bound in Silk (4 pieces: every 4th full-weight weapon hit on the same enemy deals 60 to 140% more damage) and Mephala's Veil (6 pieces: a hit that drops the wearer below 30% health gives Chameleon for 10 seconds, recovering in 4 minutes)

Questlines: The Thirteenth of Frostfall is a festival questline from Morwen, a Wyrd Sister of Glenmoril, opening at level 6, online with a registered account, while the festival runs, with a Wyrd Sister handing over Morwen's letter or her raven bringing it if a star is held first, and a step that is still going when the festival ends waits and picks up where it stood

Questlines: in The Thirteenth of Frostfall the player holds a fallen star, faces the Coven on the Bluff, then holds three more stars to earn the Starwarden title and 30 Soul Cakes, shown in the Wyrd Sisters' window once held
Questlines: holding the Heart-Star during Three Stars is an optional objective that pays more and adds Morwen's Heart-Star Ring to the choice of reward

Questlines: at the end of The Thirteenth of Frostfall the player decides what becomes of the Spinner's spindle: burn it in Hircine's fire, sell it to the Mages Guild or take it to a priest of Arkay at Arkay's own temple, each choice with its own reward
Compass: the compass on the Enhanced HUD shows the Sea Serpent and a found Abyss Dungeon, both marks having been dropped before they reached it
Hearth Offerings: interacting in a town where a player has set out a Hearth Offering no longer crashes the game, which happened whatever was interacted with there: a body, a door or a person
Hearth Offerings: in those towns the names under the crosshair show again and Hearth Offerings work: taking a Soul Cake from someone else's, or filling or taking in one's own
Questlines: each new questline's opening letter waits until the last one has reached the player, and an hour of the character's time after it, instead of letters arriving in a heap
Quests: a quest giver placed in a Mages Guild hall no longer stands inside the guild's own quest-giver
World Map: when a townsperson marks a building on the map it can be seen from the world map too, and in a town the world map has a tab for the town's streets
Town Map: on a crowded town map a name with no room is drawn as a star, and pointing at the star shows the building's name, so a marked building always shows
Town Layouts: trees in towns no longer grow around fountains, wells and crates, and a tree that stands close to one is drawn smaller
Cooking: Raw Fish in the Materials Bag can be cooked over a fire, the cooked fish going into the pack
Joinery: the joinery's carpenter, signboard and workbench all open the workbench with its craft buttons, where the carpenter and the signboard opened it with the Workbench marked as away
Stores: putting goods in the Stores no longer locks the buttons for a long time, everything put in at once being saved once instead of once a material
Stores: Temper at the Anvil and Temper at the Loom are back on the Stores page
Ship Handling: after a journey across the sea the ship stops instead of rowing on by itself, which happened when the helm was left on oars without full sails
Harbours: port towns along the coast that had no harbour now have one, including Daggerfall, Sentinel and Wayrest, and a harbour can stand a little way from its town where the shore lies far out
Tutorials: sailing from one port to another counts at every port, so the Under Sail tutorial completes
Ships at Sea: going below to the ship's cabin is not allowed while enemies are nearby, where going below made pirates vanish

Overworld: the Overworld shows the land out to the horizon, the haze over sunny and cloudy skies thinning out to where the land meets the sky instead of closing a few kilometres out, and the camera can tilt up to look along it, down to 15 degrees from 30
Overworld: clouds' shadows carry on out to the far hills, with no straight edge where they used to stop
Overworld: land seen in the distance can be clicked to travel there, where it answered "That lies beyond what you can see from here."
Overworld: while nearby land is still loading, distant hills fill the gap instead of open sky

Loading: loading into the world does less work: the longest freeze while the world is built is about half as long, the map of Tamriel is fitted in a fraction of the time and the roads' travellers are planned faster, thanks to joaomdb3's TRIP-PICKS (#854)

Trading: a shop or a trade with another player opens with its item pictures in place instead of rebuilding the window once per picture, a click on an item answers in about 50 ms where it took up to 0.8 s, buying or selling a piece takes about 0.1 s where it took up to 3 s and long lists keep their place while scrolling

Performance: Oblivion Gates, the Elite Gates' fight, the glint on gathering nodes, the sea's effects, spell impacts and the snow on the ground compile their shaders in the background instead of freezing the game for each one, each effect appearing a moment later, and on most graphics cards the gate and node effects start compiling during loading

Snowfall: the weather's snow no longer costs about 18 ms a frame, with spikes past 60 ms, while the snow on the ground catches up with the weather, keeping to its 3 ms and letting the snowline settle in over a few seconds

Discord Reports: if the player was the only one who entered the breach, the Discord announcement of a tenth Redoubt (10, 20, 30...) names them and says they did it alone, where it said "Mara's company took..." however many people were in the breach, and "The way below a band is open" uses the same wording for one player

Discord Reports: a group is still announced as a company, and anyone who stepped through counts even if they fell, went home or left, with the announcement naming someone who actually went in, never an opener who stayed outside
Elite Gates: once the first hall wakes, the company tracker counts only the people who came in, so a party member who was called but never stepped through no longer shows as part of the company

Elite Gates: in an Athenaeum the Orrery's six stones stand in the hall, each with a dial, a hand showing its hour and two levers, the right turning the stone forward and the left turning it back, where each stone was a gold ring on the floor and the turn had to be searched for in the empty air beside it
Elite Gates: the door at the end of a span no longer stays shut when the player stops to time their jumps, which made the Spire lose sight of the crossing
Elite Gates: if the door will not let the player through, it says why and what to do

Elite Gates: damage numbers on Spire lords and enemies show the damage each hit actually did, a moment after it lands, adding up to the fight's damage chart, and damage over time and Arcane Echo repeats show their numbers, a follow-up blow (Open Hand, Many Endings) being counted in its blow's number

Class Skill Swap: repeating a class skill change on the Growth tab could push the level far past what any class can reach (one class reached level 223), so a skill's training now leaves the class with it: level and progress still never drop, but after giving up a trained skill for a less trained one the class skills make up the difference before the next level comes any closer
Class Skill Swap: the swap form tells how many points that is, beside the picks and again when it asks to confirm

Townspeople: asking around for work no longer sends you to "someone named ." at "a place called ." after you've taken (or turned down) a job, or after loading a save. The answer always names a person who has work and the place to find them.
Townspeople: a woman with work for you is now "her" in those answers, not "him".

Quests: a quest that sends you to a temple or a guild hall now always names it. The Orrery of Endings, and other questline steps that began while you were out on the road, used to say things like "at in Daggerfall" with the name missing. Quests already in your journal get their names back the next time you load.
Quests: a palace a quest picks while you are on the road now has its proper name (Castle Daggerfall, Castle Wayrest, Castle Sentinel) instead of just "Palace".

Hunting: you can now skin the Enemy Expansion's animals. Bats give Bat Leather, blood spiders Spider Silk, mountain lions Tiger Pelts and land dreugh Dreugh Shells. Wolves, snow wolves and dogs give the new Wolf Pelt, boars the new Boar Hide, and mudcrabs the new Mudcrab Chitin.
Hunting: all three new hides cure to Cured Leather, and Wolf Pelts and Boar Hides make Large and Small Skins at the loom.

Arcane Essence: if you take apart a piece you crafted with materials from your pack, its Arcane Essence no longer says "bought with gold". It now shows as "made from pack goods", and the Reforge with Essence can use it. Essence already in your Stores has been corrected.
Arcane Essence: the Stores page no longer says Arcane Essence can go to your pack.

Soul Trap: a Soul Gem holding the soul of one of the Enemy Expansion's creatures (an Ogre, a Goblin, a Troll and the rest) no longer freezes your trading. If trapping one froze yours, that hold and the strikes it added are lifted.

Player Trade: in a trade with another player, an item that cannot be traded now tells you so when you offer it. Before, it sat on your side of the table while the other player saw nothing, and a trade could finish without it ever reaching them.

Wrothgarian Zone: when a player dies in the Wrothgarian Mountains, all the gold they drop now shows in their remains. Before, a drop of more than 65,535 gold never appeared, and no one could pick it up.

Wrothgarian Zone: taking only part of the gold from someone's remains, because your pack can't hold it all, now leaves the rest showing. Before, the pile could show less gold than was really there, or lose it from view.
Tab Key: pressing Tab no longer moves the keyboard onto the Social button or any other on-screen button.
Social: clicking Social, Chat, Show or "Play online here" no longer leaves that button selected, so your next jump no longer opens the friends panel again.
Overworld: when you come down from the Overworld, the grass around you no longer freezes the game while it grows back.
Overworld: crossing into a new region (desert, mountains, swamp, snow) no longer stalls the game while its ground is prepared.
Blood: the first time you take a hit, the blood on your screen no longer causes a freeze.
Overworld: long journeys hitch less often overall: the grass, the snow on the ground and the weather now create far less garbage, so the game stops much less often to clean it up.
Grass: at the edge of a snowline, grass is now buried by snow on the same slopes the snow is drawn on.

Snow: steep mountainsides keep their snow in winter. The straight green band up snowy ranges is gone: a steep face is now white like the rest of the slope. (Faces steeper than 50° still grow no trees, as in Daggerfall Unity.)
Snow: turning "Weather as places" or "Enhanced environments" on or off mid-game now redraws the ground properly, instead of leaving squares wearing the other setting's season.
Revenant Missions: online, a mission keeps real time: it keeps going while you're logged off. A day abroad is 2 real hours. Resting, waiting or traveling still doesn't speed it up.
Revenant Missions: online, a mission's time left is shown in real minutes and hours.
Hunting: making Cured Leather from mixed hides now uses Wolf Pelts and Boar Hides before Bear Hides, so your Bear Hides stay for Ram Kits.
Stores: the Stores say "3 Mudcrab Chitin", like "3 Scorpion Chitin".

Sailing: sails work again after loading a save. A save made in a dungeon or building kept the indoors' calm, and a load that woke you outdoors (online, a dungeon save always wakes you at a temple or town) brought it out to sea: under sail your ship drifted while the oars still rowed. A load outdoors now has the outdoors' wind.

Passage Under Sail: "Under Sail" counts your voyage in any boat. A slow boat - a rowboat, or a Large Boat in a light wind - had its departure counted from the edge of the harbour instead of the quay, so short trips down the coast never counted. The voyage now counts from where you last lay still.
Passage Under Sail: running aground in the next harbour, or leaving the helm as you come in, now counts as making port.
Passage Under Sail: a voyage survives a reload or a crash between the two ports.
Passage Under Sail: Pencart's harbour can be reached (its water had all been counted as Longham's).
Passage Under Sail: the harbourmaster now says what counts: the harbour of another port a quarter league off or more. "The Packet Lanes" says the same.
Lantern: a lantern lit with O (or Use, or the hotbar) shows in the Lantern slot, where it hangs at your hip - not on the shield's panel.
Lantern: O lights the lantern in your Lantern slot first, a hung lantern lights with both hands full, and the hotbar's lantern no longer takes your shield off.
Snowfall: fixed a memory leak in winter snow: every map area you travelled through stayed in memory, about 1.8 MB each - long journeys could run the game out of memory.
Loading: fixed a rare stall where the world stopped loading new ground for the rest of the session (offline play, about one area in 37).

Desktop App: on the desktop app, a game that stops now says so and why, and offers Restart, instead of leaving a black window. A game that stops responding offers Wait or Restart. The reason is kept in crash.log beside your saves - please include it in a bug report.

Witches' Festival: Soul Cakes have a daily limit of 120, and the game now tells you when you reach it and the time more can be found (midnight UTC, shown in your own time). The Wyrd Sister's window shows how many you have found today.

Starfall: each wave at a fallen star is now larger, and it grows as the fight goes on. Alone you face 4, 5, 6 and then 7 foes. Every player beside you adds two more. A group of four faces 10 to 13 a wave, a group of eight 18 to 21, and the largest waves reach 24.
Starfall: the coven's foes are tougher: its waves and the master's circle have twice their usual health. The master is unchanged.
Starfall: the coven's breath between waves is now 5 seconds, down from 12.
Starfall: waves now gather just outside the crater instead of far beyond it, so they reach you sooner.
Starfall: in a group, a wave you clear quickly now ends when you clear it. Before, a large group could stand in an empty crater for up to a minute.
Starfall: the mound of earth around a fallen star's crater is now solid. You can no longer walk through it. You also can't get stuck in it if the crater forms around you.
Premade Classes: barbarian: primaries Axe, Blunt Weapon and Critical Strike; majors Long Blade, Dodging and Running (were Jumping, Running and Swimming).
Premade Classes: acrobat: gains Short Blade as a primary and Archery as a major.
Premade Classes: Mage and Sorcerer are no longer identical. Both lead with Destruction, the Sorcerer adds Blunt Weapon, and neither spends skill slots on Dragonish or Daedric.
Premade Classes: healer: Blunt Weapon is now a major.
Premade Classes: archer: Critical Strike replaces Hand-to-Hand as a primary; Short Blade, Long Blade and Stealth are its majors.
Premade Classes: Warrior, Barbarian: two weapons and Critical Strike as primaries, so every swing trains both the weapon in hand and Critical Strike.
Premade Classes: no class spends a skill slot on a language. Languages are still learnable.
Premade Classes: Burglar can now wear leather armour (it is forbidden chain and plate instead of leather and chain).
Enemy Sync: in busy areas, other players' enemies no longer die for one player and stay alive for another, or vanish when the player who controls them leaves, dies or goes through a door.
Starfall: at a crowded Starfall, every player's enemies now reach everyone in turn - including the player who controls the star's waves, whose enemies could go unseen by others before.
Enemy Sync: enemies controlled by a slow or lagging player now move smoothly for everyone else instead of freezing and jumping.
Enemy Sync: on a slow computer with other players nearby, enemies keep pace with your character instead of moving at half speed - outdoors, in buildings and in dungeons, and the town watch with them.
Ships at Sea: ships far out at sea, other players' boats and your own moored boats far away cost much less to draw.
Horse: horses - other players', strangers' on the road and those standing in towns - are only animated in full when you can see them, and a horse that comes into view is drawn in its current stride.
Grass: grass no longer stutters while riding or running fast on a slower computer, and fills in around you even when you arrive at speed.
Sea: the ocean no longer stays nearly black after sunrise and before sunset; it brightens along with the sky.
Guilds: a guild can now hold 75 members (up from 50).
Grass: grass sways more gently in the wind. Blades lean less than half as far at a full gust, and gusts roll through the field more softly instead of whipping it.
Wisps: the wind wisps are more transparent and shorter. You can still see which way the wind blows, but they no longer stand out against the scenery.

Abyss Dungeons: once anyone steps through an Abyss Dungeon's Rift, a portal - the Way Through - opens beside everyone in the dungeon, and beside everyone who enters it afterwards. Use it to go straight to the Shattered Hour.
Abyss Dungeons: the Way Through closes when the Brass Remnant falls.

Online Sign-In: signing in, and joining the world, failed for many players for an hour or two after midnight UTC every night. The game no longer has every player's client check in with the server in the same second when the day changes. Each client now waits a random 0–10 minutes past midnight.
Gathering Nodes: for those few minutes after midnight, the ground's gathering nodes, your profession's day and the town reports stay on the day before's until your client catches up. Nothing is lost.
Morrowind People: a yellow "!" over anyone a quest needs, including the townsfolk who've been named as having work for you.
Morrowind People: an amber coin over merchants: shopkeepers, bankers and innkeepers.
Morrowind People: a blue gem over guild trainers, spell sellers and quest givers, the witches' coven, and the arena's officers.

Morrowind People: walls hide the markers, and they fade out beyond about 30 metres. Classic sprites don't get one, because their picture already tells you who they are. Turn them off with Morrowind People Marks on the Features page.
